Sports.title: Man Utd put four past Sabah on Champions League return
Sports.content:
Manchester United made a winning return to the Champions League as they beat Sabah FC in style with a 4-0 victory at Old Trafford.

The Azerbaijani side started brightly but Matheus Cunha converted Patrick Dorgu's 27th-minute cross and, although Joy-Lance Mickels should have levelled, two goals late in the first half from Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko put United in total control.

Michael Carrick made changes in the second half with the points secure but there was still time for Lisandro Martinez to smash home from close range after some flashy play from Joshua Zirkzee, who produced an eye-catching cameo. Signs of that United swagger.

With goal difference a potentially significant factor in the league phase of this Champions League format, this was a fine night's work on their return. It is Atletico Madrid away next in Europe but there are bigger matters to attend to before that.

Analysis: Carrick has options

It is over 1000 days since United competed in a Champions League game but this, their 300th in Europe's premier club competition, was not too taxing for Carrick's men. It will be tougher against rivals Manchester City on Sunday - but so will his team selection.

Some of the calls are obvious. Fernandes starred again and the sight of him combining with the equally intelligent Youri Tielemans for United's second was encouraging. The Belgian produced perhaps his best 45 minutes at Old Trafford. But others pressed their case too.

Image: Youri Tielemans celebrates with Bruno Fernandes during the win over Sabah

Sesko scored after coming off the bench against Everton and looked sharp here in his first start of the season. With Marcus Rashford also available, and Cunha getting a confidence-boosting goal, there are some interesting decisions ahead for the United boss.

Dorgu enjoyed himself at left-back with Luke Shaw missing from the squad but he was able to play as a de facto winger given United's superiority. It will be more challenging against City's attack but Carrick and his players go into that with confidence restored.

The key moments from Old Trafford

27 - GOAL! Cunha converts Dorgu's cross at the near post

36 - SITTER! Mickels nods wide from inside the six-yard box

42 - GOAL! Fernandes makes it two from Tielemans' pass

45 - GOAL! Mbeumo puts Sesko in to round the goalkeeper

68 - GOAL! Zirkzee's backheel finds Martinez who smashes it in

Carrick: Really encouraging

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick speaking in the press conference:

"I think it was kind of what we set out to achieve, good performance, individually and collectively throughout the game, the boys that started, the boys that came on pitch, clean sheet, goals, exciting football. A good night all round.

"Results-wise, it has not been the start that what we wanted. We wanted more points in the league. But performance-wise, it has been a lot of things we are looking for.

"Collectively, as a team, we have done a lot of the right things and that is why were are excited about what the season will bring. It is really encouraging for me."

On the performance of Benjamin Sesko…

"He definitely offers a different kind of threat, that is the beauty of it really, we know what Ben gives us and there are not many who can give us what he gives us. Speed, physicality, ability to play on the last line and run in behind. Great to have him back."

Dambrauskas: Almost impossible to stop

Sabah head coach Valdas Dambrauskas speaking in the press conference:

"I didn't feel like we were shaking or scared, we tried to play, for the whole 90 minutes we did that. We were escaping from time to time from United pressure.

"We will all go home thinking we could have done better, especially the result. The result could have been a little bit smaller.

"We did not have enough courage probably from the back line to get up. Our centre-backs stayed too deep, not afraid but maybe from inexperience we were over-evaluating the opponent.

"Because when you don't squeeze that space and you allow those players to turn and run it is almost impossible to stop them."

What is next for Man Utd...

Sports.title: McIlroy four off Irish Open lead in tough conditions with Lowry near top
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy battled on against testing blustery conditions at the Amgen Irish Open to sit four shots off the clubhouse lead following a one-under par opening round, with Ireland's Shane Lowry two off the top.

Gusts up to 35mph saw balls oscillating on greens with Frenchman Frederic Lacroix seeing his blown off the putting surface at the 13th, but he had fortunately already marked so was able to replace it.

All of which made for slow going at Trump International Golf Links and Hotel in Doonbeg during Thursday's first round.

As the day wore on, a course-record 65 from Chilean Joaquin Niemann looked increasingly good.

Having reached the turn at two under, Niemann had four successive birdies from the 14th to put him in contention for a $30,000 (£22,000) bonus for the lowest round of the week.

Austrian Maximilian Steinlechner and Renato Paratore appeared set to make a challenge for the top of the leaderboard at three under through 12 and 11 respectively, but could be thwarted by the fading light.

Home favourite Lowry, who won the event as a 22-year-old amateur in Baltray, kept himself in the mix, also in the clubhouse at three under.

Image: Ireland's Lowry sits two shots off the lead following the opening round

Long waits on many tee boxes had been commonplace but McIlroy, who had won the event at the K Club last year, started with two birdies in his first four holes before getting to the turn in a two-under 34 - in three and a half hours.

After missing a four-foot birdie chance at the first he holed a 14-footer at the second, splashed out of a bunker to three feet at the par-five fourth for his second birdie, but missed from 10 feet at the seventh for a third.

McIlroy found the fairway bunker on the 13th, and a missed 10-foot putt saw him take a double-bogey hit before a fine approach to the 15th helped quickly pull a stroke back.

The world No 2, though, could not make the most of what proved limited opportunities over the closing run, narrowly missing a lengthy birdie attempt on the 18th, and will return on Friday morning hoping to improve along with the weather forecast.

"This course isn't conducive to sort of letting you get in a flow. Especially the first two days with so many people in the field, there is a lot of stopping and starting.

Sports.title: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return
Sports.content:
It was a night for romance given the astonishing story that Sabah brought with them to Old Trafford for their Champions League debut. This is a club that did not even exist a decade ago and nobody saw their bolt to the title in Azerbaijan coming last season; in 2024-25, they had finished 41 points off the top. The job that their manager, Valdas Dambrauskas, has done since taking over in the summer of last year is extraordinary.

It was also a night for cold, hard reality. Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.

Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City.

United had wanted to put their best foot forward when they heard the Champions League aria after the chaos and embarrassment of their previous involvement in the competition. Erik ten Hag was the manager in 2023-24 and his team finished bottom of their group with four points, starting and ending with losses to Bayern Munich. It was what happened in between times against Galatasaray and Copenhagen that still causes a few shudders. It was a period when United panicked uncontrollably when they had a lead. When the defensive gifts from them came in crazy clusters.

Carrick took no chances with his starting XI. There was minimal rotation in the midfield and front line, save for a first start of the season for Sesko in the No 9 position. It was easy to think that the manager wanted to groove Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo in central midfield before the City game.

United looked to Fernandes to get them going. As always. There were intelligent runs from him; incision about his passes, that wonderful disguise on some of them. The breakthrough goal stemmed from him chasing a high ball over the top that looked like a lost cause only for him to keep it in play. It was what happened next that quickened United pulses. When Sabah gave the ball away cheaply to Bryan Mbeumo, United moved quickly over to the left. Patrick Dorgu crossed and Cunha’s finish was clean.

Sabah lined up in a 4-3-3 formation; no bus parking. They wanted to ask questions of a United defence that had a makeshift feel about it. There was assurance on the ball from them, the desire to carry it forward. And a huge chance in the 35th minute when Kaheem Parris crossed to the back post. Joy-Lance Mickels was clear of Noussair Mazraoui only to put the header wide. The angle was not favourable. It did not entirely excuse him.

View image in fullscreen Matheus Cunha opens the scoring with a smart finish in the first half. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

Sabah were harshly treated by the half-time scoreline, even though United played on the front foot and created openings. It was the one-two punch in the closing stages of the first period that changed everything. Fernandes – who else? – made a sidefoot finish look easy after Tielemans had burst on a Cunha pass inside, spun and teed him up. The third followed a first time pass by Fernandes into Mbeumo, who got Sesko clean though. The Sabah backline was high. Sesko went around the goalkeeper to score. He never looked like missing.

There was a lovely scene 90 ­minutes before kick-off when some of the Sabah players wandered around the pitch, the stadium virtually empty, phones out to capture the quiet before the storm, the sheer scale of Old Trafford. They wore wide smiles. They were determined not to be overawed when it got started. The performance of the strolling central midfielder, Ivan Lepinjica, was certainly impressive. They were just too loose at the back.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United played some slick stuff at times, Mainoo and ­Fernandes ever involved. When Carrick’s ­pass-and-move game clicks, it is easy to feel the ­possibility. ­Imposing it against the higher-­profile teams is the name of the game. ­Starting against City.

Mason Mount was introduced at half-time for his first football of the season – “It was great to get Mason back on the pitch,” Carrick later said – with Tielemans coming off, his work done. The Belgian could be pleased with his impact. Carrick was always going to withdraw other likely starters against City, such as Mainoo. Sesko came off with him on 64 minutes and was warmly applauded. After his goal at Everton on Sunday, has he done enough to make the XI for the derby?

Carrick added: “We always push for more. Results-wise it hasn’t been the start we wanted, but performance-wise there are a lot of things we were looking for. The clean sheet was important tonight. Collectively as a team we have done a lot of good things and that is why we are excited what this season can bring.”

His side controlled the second half. The jeopardy was long gone. The fourth goal summed up Sabah’s travails in their defensive third. It was a scooped free-kick by Fernandes for Joshua Zirkzee, on as a substitute, and when his backheel hit Aden ­McCarthy, the Sabah goalkeeper, Stas Pokatilov, lost his bearings, the ball caught under his feet. It was a tap-in for Martínez. The substitute, Orphé Mbina, headed high for Sabah at the very end. There was to be no fairytale goal.

Sports.title: Clearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter
Sports.content:
Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital, are closing in on an agreement to buy out co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in a deal that would see the pair make a profit on their investment and value the club at around £5bn.

On-off discussions between the two ownership groups over a potential sale have been taking place for the last two years, but intensified last month as a result of Mark Walter seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers following a US federal investigation over alleged tax fraud.

Walter, Boehly and Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss all own 12.8% of Chelsea following their joint £2.5bn purchase of the club with Clearlake from Roman Abramovich four years ago, in a deal in which the new owners commit to spending a further £1.75bn on the club.

Under the terms of their ownership agreement, none of Chelsea’s shareholders can sell to a third party without the consent of their partners giving Clearlake, whose investment is managed by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, an exclusive option to purchase Boehly and Walter’s stakes.

In a statement issued to Bloomberg a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he is seeking a sale with an agreement close. Boehly is also expected to sell as he is a long-time investment partner of Walters. Wyss’s position is unconfirmed.

“This potential transaction values Mark Walter’s stake in Chelsea Football Club at a premium to his initial investment and is another successful sports investment for him,” a spokesperson for Walter said.

“After this exit, Mr Walter intends to make future sports-related investments. “Walter did not initiate the proposed transaction to sell his interest, which has been in the works for quite some time.”

As 61.5% shareholders, Clearlake already had day-to-day operational control at Chelsea managed by Eghbali, and were due to make their own appointment as chairman to replace Boehly next year, but taking complete control will ease internal tensions at the club and should smooth decision making.

The most immediate impact of the impending ownership change is likely to be felt in Chelsea’s plans for a new stadium, as Eghbali has clashed with Boehly over whether the club should seek to redevelop Stamford Bridge or seek an alternative site elsewhere.

Walter is being investigated by the US Department of Justice over $21bn in loans which it has been alleged were not disclosed to state insurance regulators, and led to the sudden sale of assets to pay down some of the loans.

The American insurance and sports investor last month sold his 85% stake in the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh ⁠Kushner and Bob Iger in a deal that valued the NBA franchise at around £9bn.

Walter’s holding company, TWG Global, subsequently issued a statement saying that the company “is not looking to sell its sports assets at ‘fire sale’ prices”.

Representatives for Boehly and Clearlake declined to comment.

Sports.title: French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support
Sports.content:
The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election.

The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to “events during the World Cup” which had “flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run” and to Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash.

During the World Cup the suspension of the US forward Folarin Balogun was overturned by Fifa after lobbying from Donald Trump. The US president said he called Infantino to recommend that Balogun be allowed to play. Fifa has said the decision taken by its disciplinary committee was “a balanced measure” and “based on an explicit provision of the applicable regulations”.

Diallo outlined the reasons for the loss in confidence: “From July onwards, the conditions which led to us to support his candidacy had been disrupted. Does the withdrawal of the [sell-off] project solve the issue? I don’t think so. His initiatives during and after the World Cup have seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”

Diallo said of the initial decision to support Infantino: “It would be wrong to say that certain developments in football were not made under his mandate.” But he added: “When you are making changes to the game itself, in a unilateral and opaque fashion to sell our shared asset, that changes our appreciation.

“France is one of the founding members of Fifa, and as such we have a historical legitimacy to intervene when we feel that Fifa and its president are deviating from our vision of how world football should be run. We also have sporting legitimacy, as one of the top three teams in the world rankings over the last 10 years. We wanted to make it clear that we refuse to go in a direction which does not correspond to the general interest of our sport.”

When reports of the sell-off project came to light, the FFF expressed “doubts and deep concerns”. Uefa threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions and several European countries, including Wales and England, withdrew their support for Infantino but the FFF had not until Thursday publicly disavowed him.

Diallo indicated France would play an active part in Uefa’s search for an alternative candidate for the Fifa presidency before the 18 November deadline. The election will take place in March during Fifa’s next congress.

Before then, Diallo said, the FFF would reach out to figures it considers experts in “transparency and good governance” in football and beyond as part of France’s “contribution to the debate”, as it pushes for “far-reaching reform” of Fifa.

He cited Kevin Lamour, the former Fifa chief operating officer who was dismissed after criticising the sell-off plan, as one of the people the FFF would look to consult.

Sports.title: Champions League: Bayern break down Bodø/Glimt, Como put four past Leipzig
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich opened their Champions League campaign with a 5-0 thrashing of Norway’s Bodo/Glimt.

The six-times winners were frustrated before half-time by Bodo/Glimt but cruised once Jamal Musiala smashed in the opener two minutes into the second period and the floodgates opened.

Harry Kane headed the second on the hour – his 34th goal in 39 Champions League appearances for Bayern – and Alphonso Davies made it 3-0 with a powerful half-volley. With Vincent Kompany’s side in full flow, Michael ‌Olise completed the scoring with a superb late brace.

Cesc Fàbregas’s Como impressed on their debut in Europe’s premier club competition, crushing RB Lepzig 4-1.

Goals from Croatia midfielder Martin Baturina, Greece forward Tasos Douvikas and Senegal’s Assane Diao put Como in control. Serbia midfielder Andrija Maksimović pulled a goal back for Leipzig, before Maximo Perrone sealed a 4-1 victory late on in a dream night in northern Italy.

View image in fullscreen Como manager Cesc Fàbregas gives a post-game, on-pitch team talk to his players after opening the Italian side’s Champions League campaign with a win. Photograph: Alex Pantling/UEFA/Getty Images

Ten-man Slavia Prague suffered ​heartbreak at home to Lens ‌as they conceded twice in ​stoppage time to lose 3-2.

Mikulas ​Konecny was sent off for the hosts just after half-time after a tackle was reviewed by VAR, but minutes later Danijel Sturm put the hosts ahead. Abdallah Sima broke Slavia’s resistance with an equaliser only for Sturm to send the home crowd into raptures with his second in the 88th minute.

Florian Thauvin struck in the 91st minute and there was still time for Lens to snatch victory with a pinpoint strike by Ruben Aguilar.

PSV came from a goal down to draw 1-1 at home to Shakhtar Donetsk and end a woeful record in their opening matches of Champions League campaigns. The Dutch club had lost their opening fixtures in their last five Champions League appearances and trailed at half-time before Sergiño Dest ensured a point.

Right near the end of a cagey first half, Shakhtar stunned the hosts when Gleiker Mendoza cut in from wide and ‌sent a stunning low ‌shot beyond the dive of Matej Kovar. PSV responded immediately after the break as the ‌ball was fed across the area to Dest who calmly found the bottom corner with an inch-perfect shot.

Roma drew 1-1 with Fenerbahce in Istanbul, with Bryan Cristante’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Archie Brown’s goal three minutes into the second half. Confusion reigned after the match as the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation – only for the club president to insist he will stay.

Sports.title: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay
Sports.content:
The Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League – but minutes ⁠later, the club ⁠president ​said Kartal would stay in the job.

Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leaving Fenerbahce “never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks.

Minutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it,” the club president added.

“I just spoke to Ismail Kartal. He mentioned the bottle incident and he also complained about being under pressure,” he continued. Asked whether the manager had told him he would stay, Yildirim said: “There’s no need for him ‌to say that he’d continue. I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s ​it. We are a family.”

Kartal, who spent a decade at Fenerbahce as a player, coached the club in 2014-15, then on an interim basis in 2021-22 before returning for a full ⁠campaign in 2023-24. He was the assistant manager at Fenerbahce the ​last two ​times the club won ​the Turkish title, and returned for a fourth ​managerial spell in ‌June.

View image in fullscreen Archie Brown celebrates his equaliser for Fenerbahce. The English full-back was left dumbfounded when learning of his coach’s resignation after the final whistle. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Fenerbahce have ​finished second ​in the Turkish Super Lig in each of the last five seasons, and reached the Champions League’s group phase this season for the first time in 18 years. The team sit ninth in the Turkish top-flight, having lost twice in their opening four games, including Saturday’s 2-1 home defeat to Besiktas.

Roma took the lead in the 39th minute when Donyell Malen rolled a pass to ​Bryan Cristante, who beat Fenerbahce keeper Ederson with a bouncing finish. The hosts levelled before half-time when Mason Greenwood slipped a ​pass through to Archie ​Brown, who clipped a finish over ​Mile Svilar.

Roma were awarded a penalty in the 68th minute when ​Karem Akturkoglu was ‌penalised for a ​foul on Paulo ​Dybala, but a VAR check ruled that the challenge had taken place outside the area. Fenerbahce came closest to grabbing a winner late on when Nathan Aké headed against the Roma crossbar.

Fenerbahce will travel to Aston Villa and host Liverpool in two of their remaining league phase games – whether Kartal will be in charge or not remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Why Kai Havertz’s dummy was perhaps more pleasing than a Lionel Messi waltz | Max Rushden
Sports.content:
During Covid, when sport was back but behind closed doors, I hosted a number of strange online shows to fill the void of real life. The highlight was chatting to Darren Gough about a lifesize bronze rhinoceros for 45 minutes to 15 small boxes on a Zoom call. I don’t recall who it was for and where the rhinoceros came from – but it might be in his garden.

I ended up doing virtual pre-match corporate Zoom calls for Heineken before Europa League games. It was the wifi version of Club Wembley: a Q&A happening on stage between a generic host and some random ex-pro while you’re trying to chat to your mate and eat an unidentified square of meat with some dauphinoise potatoes.

I’d be in my little square talking to Luis García in his little square about the ghost goal while an assorted group of faces and living rooms or kitchen tables would stare at you, perhaps interested, perhaps not. Did they even want to be there? Were we on mute while someone from marketing was filling a spare box on my laptop watching Death In Paradise on the TV behind me?

Certainly it was hard to create an amazing vibe with Mark van Bommel while his internet connection crashed and a little note on a Google doc appeared telling me to fill for 25 minutes with my favourite memories of the Europa League. Did these disembodied heads in front of me want the deep dive they got on Tony Parks’ heroics in 1984? How many of them knew about Gary Mabbutt playing centre mid and marking Enzo Scifo out of the game?

One of the guests was Dimitar Berbatov. You’d log on half an hour before the show and say hello, try to build some kind of electric rapport with a man in Bulgaria (I think) presumably looking to get in and get out and get back on with whatever social distancing life in Sofia had to offer.

He may have not had Akabusi levels of energy, and his economy of language was not unlike his playing style – why use a hundred words when one will do? But he was into it and did the job perfectly. I absolutely loved Berbatov as a player. Watching him pluck a goalkick out of the sky was more beautiful than watching a lot of other players banging one in from 25 yards. There’s a YouTube video called Dimitar Berbatov – the most underrated first touch ever? It begins with him standing like a lamp-post on the halfway line at Craven Cottage and stopping a crossfield ball stone dead like it’s an anvil.

View image in fullscreen Dimitar Berbatov, pictured scoring for Manchester United against Sunderland in 2009, could make football look easy. Photograph: Carl Recine/Action Images/Reuters

Back to the Zoom call: I welcome Dimitar, he says hello, I explain my admiration for him, and then say to him that he made football look easy. Did he find it easy? “Yes” he replied. Totally matter of fact. Not trying to impress – just explaining that football was easy.

And for someone like Berbatov, it is a different level to “good touch for a big man”. This is the ultimate type of grace on a football pitch. And perhaps it is reserved for tall, skilful players. I’ve probably used the word languid already but I can’t think of any other use of the word – reserved for players who are almost balletic.

Is it insane to say it’s more aesthetically pleasing than seeing a Messi or a Maradona waltz through a defence? It almost feels as if a low centre of gravity gives you an unfair advantage when it comes to technical skill. No flailing arms and legs to get in the way of you being naturally brilliant.

View image in fullscreen Argentina’s Lionel Messi dribbles away from three Dutch players in the 2022 World Cup. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

My biased brain instantly goes to Glenn Hoddle walking through the Oxford United defence with one sway, sitting the keeper down with a movement of the leg. It’s all saying: “This is easier for me than it is for you.”

Which brings us to Kai Havertz – and that dummy against Chelsea. The more and more football becomes that David Mitchell sketch, the more surprised I am that there are still moments in a game that lead to some involuntary noise from deep within.

The ball from Christos Tzolis is definitely for him. Havertz points in front to where he wants the ball. If it’s played there he can probably get a shot away first time. But when it comes, controlling the ball would have been a sensible choice. Back to goal. He could have turned and shot, or just kept the ball. There are lots of good players to pass it to.

View image in fullscreen Martin Ødegaard scores Arsenal’s second goal against Chelsea after Kai Havertz’s dummy. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Even the way he lifts his left leg at the last second to let the ball run through to Martin Ødegaard is delightful. It’s easy to forget the pace of the game at this level. And when you’re watching on TV where it’s much easier to see the pass you also forget these guys don’t have that view.

Someone somewhere will have done a report on Havertz’s scanning abilities. He doesn’t appear to look behind to check where Ødegaard is. But awareness is hard to calculate. He just knows. And he does it all in a split second, not even. How wonderful that you can do so much without even touching the ball.

A lot of people do quite well out of repeatedly asking whether Arsenal need a centre-forward, so I don’t want to do them out of work. And Havertz isn’t perfect – he isn’t Robbie Fowler in the box. But he has scored in two Champions League finals. He did win the league last season. A lot of beautiful graceful players tend to be beautiful and graceful without delivering on the biggest occasions. Havertz does both. And when he gets it right, it looks easy to him. Imagine finding it easy.

Sports.title: Declan Rice shrugs off Arsenal concerns and says 60 games a season is sustainable
Sports.content:
Declan Rice has insisted his body can sustain more than 60 appearances again this season, despite Arsenal’s concerns after he played through pain at the World Cup.

Rice racked up 69 appearances last season for Arsenal and England but revealed during the World Cup he had been managing neural back and hamstring pain, for which he is understood to have received a pain-killing injection, after a hamstring injury in December. It is understood Arsenal are monitoring the 27-year-old’s workload closely after he had only three weeks off before returning to training a week before the Community Shield last month.

Rice came off the bench to replace Bruno Guimarães in the victory over Manchester City in Cardiff and has since started all Arsenal’s matches, with Guimarães’ return from an injury being managed. A major reason why Arsenal bought the Brazil midfielder for £75m from Newcastle was to take some strain off from Rice, although it was noticeable that Rice played all of Wednesday’s Champions League victory at Napoli, with Mikel Merino coming off for Guimarães.

“I think for the last six seasons, even since my West Ham days when they were in Europe, I’ve played 60-plus every season,” Rice said. “So I think it is sustainable because I’ve shown that I can do it.

“It’s just about maintaining it, maintaining the level and the consistency of the performances. For me, that’s the main thing, showing up every week, giving a good account of myself and helping the team win. I’ve been lucky enough to be able to do that. So I’m really hungry to be able to do that again this season.”

It is understood Arsenal offered Rice more time off after the World Cup exploits but that he was keen to return for the start of the season. He is expected to be part of Thomas Tuchel’s squad for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia when it is announced next Friday, although whether he features in all four matches remains to be seen, with Arsenal likely to request that he and Bukayo Saka are given another opportunity to rest. Rice said he had found things “tough” during the World Cup but is adamant he is feeling “refreshed”.

“I feel really good at the minute, in really good form, so we’ll make it continue,” he said. “I think everyone knew I had an issue with a neural hamstring. But also on the top of the Premier League season, which was so demanding, the Champions League, to then play a World Cup in that heat really does take its toll. I’m a player that goes on the pitch, wants to be fresh and give 100% every time I put on an England shirt. Yes, there were stages where I felt really, really good and stages where I didn’t feel so good. There were a few things that frustrated me, just with myself, just not feeling 100%. It’s one of those things I just had to manage.”

Rice is one of three England players nominated for the Ballon d’Or this week, with Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane. The ceremony, traditionally in Paris, will take place in London on 26 October as a tribute to Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the inaugural award in 1956, and Rice has backed Kane to become the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001. “I would Iove to see Harry win it,” he said. “So I’m wishing him all the best in that.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Mauricio Pochettino, Tottenham’s game of thrones and retrospective action
Sports.content:
ER, MEMORY LANE?

State-sanctioned execution of spouses and allies (Henry VIII), the Marian persecutions (Mary I), and enslavement and branding of the unemployed (Edward VI). During the 15th and 16th centuries, assorted monarchs from the House of Tudor were responsible for visiting no end of dread and terror on their subjects but it is the 44-day reign of one of their more contemporary counterparts at Tottenham that local subjects found truly unforgivable. Enthroned last February to secure Spurs’ safety following the dismissal of Thomas Frank, Igor Tudor took just one point from 15 available in his five top-flight games in charge. His subsequent deposition heralded the arrival of Roberto De Zerbi and ultimately last-day Premier League survival, but may also have denied the club’s fans a reunion with Mauricio Pochettino, a comparatively beloved former monarch who was tasked with focusing on other conquests in the Americas at the time.

“The problem was that the timings were never the best,” tooted Poch of the game of thrones played out in the kingdoms of the Seven Sisters and the New World that he claims dashed his hopes of coaching at the Geopolitics World Cup and then returning to a club he had managed for more than five years. “When I was free, I never received a contact. And then when I was working [with USA USA USA], I received a contact but I cannot make the decision to come back. It was a little bit unlucky. Maybe one day the stars will align and it can happen. If I was free, of course, I come. But I wasn’t free.” Having since signed a new four-year deal, he remains with the USA USA USA, while De Zerbi is tied to Spurs until 2031. Or possibly November.

A man who famously keeps a bowl of lemons in the office to help soak up negative energy, Pochettino might have needed several silos of the citrus fruit if things had worked out differently and he’d returned to coach a Spurs side muddying their spats in the Championship. However, it is a role the former manager of Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea insists he would not have considered beneath him. “Tottenham … it’s the only club that always I am open to help in whatever division,” he cooed, when quizzed about his appetite for the grind of midweek trips to Lincoln City, Bolton and Stoke.

In a wide-ranging interview staged in That There Big London to mark the beginning of his second cycle as USA USA USA head coach, Pochettino stated that Chelsea should be stripped of the Premier League title they won in 2016-17, having since been found guilty of multiple and serious financial shenanigans at that time. As luck would have it, in such a scenario the honour would almost certainly be bestowed on a Spurs side that finished second in the league that season and happened to be coached by him. “If that [Chelsea’s chicanery] was true, then we deserve to be champions that year, for sure,” he parped. “They were punished, they admitted it? So that’s it. The title should be for the team that was second.” While Poch might well have an excellent point, Football Daily can’t say we recall him being such a stickler for the fastidious application of the rules when his USA USA USA team’s star striker had a ban controversially shelved by Fifa following the intervention of Donald Trump at the recent GWC.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Daniel Harris from 8pm BST for hot Bigger Cup minute-by-minute coverage of Manchester United 2-0 Mr Loverman Sabah ! Sabah! .

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“At that time it was quite big money. I could have bought a flat in my home town; it was a very difficult period there and they were almost free. But my plan was to go to England and follow my dream to become a coach, and that’s how it started” – Valdas Dambrauskas gets his very entertaining chat on with Nick Ames about his remarkable journey from an appearance on the Lithuanian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? via pub work in north London, to becoming manager of Azerbaijani champions Sabah.

View image in fullscreen Valdas Dambrauskas there. Photograph: Aziz Karimov/Getty Images

double quotation mark Given that Mauricio Pochettino believes the Premier League title shouldn’t go to the club that finished first in the table, he truly is a Spurs manager at heart. And, given he also says that if he were Chelsea manager at the time, he’d admit that ‘we don’t deserve the title because we broke the rules’, it also conclusively proves he was the completely wrong man for Chelsea” – Noble Francis.

double quotation mark Just because Amazon now co-owns Liverpool FC doesn’t mean it can command Alexa Alexis to score a match-winning goal in European competition, does it?!” – Peter Oh.

Todd Boehly is on the brink of leaving Chelsea and selling his minority stake - with Behdad Eghbali's Clearlake Capital set to take control of club

Behdad Eghbali and his Clearlake Capital group could soon have total control over Chelsea with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter believed to be progressing in talks to sell their minority shares.

Boehly, Walter and Hansjorg Wyss own 38.5 per cent of the Premier League club collectively. The other 61.5 per cent is held by Clearlake, who are led by Eghbali and Jose E Feliciano.

While Boehly is Chelsea chairman and was the original face of the 2022 takeover, Eghbali has been the most hands-on of all the co-owners. He often liaises with the sporting directorship team and is a consistent attendee at games both at home and away.

In a statement issued to Bloomberg, a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he is seeking a sale with an agreement close. Boehly is likewise expected to sell. Wyss’s stance is unconfirmed.

If all three agreed to an in-house sale, Boehly, Walter and Wyss would expect to make a minor profit on their original investment. The entire consortium purchased Chelsea for £2.5billion in 2022 with an additional £1.75bn committed to investment in the club.

As originally reported by Bloomberg, a spokesperson for Walter said: ‘This potential transaction values Mark Walter’s stake in Chelsea Football Club at a premium to his initial investment and is another successful sports investment for him. After this exit, Mr Walter intends to make future sports-related investments.’

Todd Boehly is believed to be progressing in talks to sell his minority share in Chelsea

Boehly's fellow minority owner Mark Walter is also doing similar, meaning Behdad Eghbali (pictured left with Boehly) and his Clearlake Capital group could have full control of the club

The spokesperson added: ‘Walter did not initiate the proposed transaction to sell his interest, which has been in the works for quite some time.’

Boehly tried his hand at being involved in transfers early on – he once admitted to buying Marc Cucurella from Brighton because Manchester City also wanted him – though Eghbali has largely led the show since that early experiment.

Reports have suggested Boehly and Eghbali held a strained relationship and there has been speculation surrounding one buying out the other for around two years now.

Sports.title: Man United make light work of minnows Sabah as Youri Tielemans excels in 4-0 win on Champions League return - but tougher tests await for Michael Carrick's men
Sports.content:
Man United make light work of minnows Sabah as Youri Tielemans excels in 4-0 win on Champions League return - but tougher tests await for Michael Carrick's men

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Until the Champions League anthem echoed around Old Trafford for the first time in nearly three years shortly before kick-off here last night, it was easy to forget that playing Sabah on a Thursday night marked Manchester United's return to Europe's top table.

With respect to the visitors from Azerbaijan, it was a fixture and a night of the week more in keeping with the UEFA Conference League.

United duly made light work of the minnows from Masazir – population 19,000 – to get their campaign off to the winning start that everyone expected and maintain a 100 per cent record among Premier League clubs in this week's first round.

The timing of the game, three days before the Old Trafford derby, was not ideal for Michael Carrick given that Manchester City had played on Tuesday.

However, a routine win and the opportunity to make changes both before and during this game with Sunday in mind was just what Carrick needed.

Safe to say, a decidedly tougher test awaits United away to Atletico Madrid in the Metropolitano next month.

Youri Tielemans (left) excelled on Manchester United's return to the Champions League

Benjamin Sesko celebrates after scoring on his first start of the season

It's difficult to judge their performance against opposition of this quality, but Youri Tielemans – whose £35million transfer fee from Aston Villa this summer could have paid for the Sabah squad twice over – excelled in midfield to help put the result beyond doubt before half-time, and Kobbie Mainoo shone alongside him.

Scorers: Cunha 27, Fernandes 42, Sesko 45, Martinez 68 Booked: Dorgu Head coach: Michael Carrick 7 SABAH FK (4-2-3-1): Pokatilov 5; Zedadka 5 (Almeida 76, 6), Dashdamiro 6, McCarthy 6.5, Puchacz 5; Rakhmonaliev 5.5 (Khaibulaev 71, 6), Lepinjica 5; Parris 7 (Isaev 63, 5.5), Simic 6 (Du Queiroz 75, 5.5), Nwachukwu 4.5 (Mbina 46, 6); Mickels 7 Subs not used: Ramazanov, Mirzammadov, Rustamli, Mutallimov, R Fernandes, Mukhtarov Booked: Lepinjica Head coach: Valdas Dambrauskas 5 Referee: Willy Delajod (France) 7 Att: 73,685

Luke Shaw, on whom so much hinges at left-back, was rested after suffering cramp in last Sunday's draw at Everton, and his replacement Patrick Dorgu posed a persistent threat going forward, even though his defensive capabilities were rarely tested.

Marcus Rashford was also left on the bench after overstretching a hamstring at the weekend, which meant that Matheus Cunha reverted to the left flank after struggling as a false nine in the opening three games, and Benjamin Sesko made his first start of the season.

Both players scored here with Sesko's second goal in four days strengthening his case to be in the line-up against City.

'Of course, I'm happy with my goal,' said the Slovenian. 'I think the confidence boost is definitely big. Now it's important to recover well and focus on the derby.'

United could hardly have chosen a more peculiar occasion for their 300th appearance in this competition. They were 1/10 on with the bookies to beat a club that didn't even exist a decade ago and had already fought through four qualifying rounds as underdogs to reach the league phase.

The story of their manager Valdas Dambrauskas, retold many times before he arrived back in Manchester, rather summed up the remarkable nature of this tie. The man who won £2,500 on Lithuania's version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? and used it to fund a coaching education which included a spell with United's Soccer Schools.

It's fair to say that education continued on a night when Sabah gave a good account of themselves but always looked second best.

'I think we learned a lot,' admitted Dambrauskas. 'We will all go home thinking we could have done a little bit better, especially with the result.

'This is massive experience for us; 16 players went on the pitch and only one of them played at this level before.'

Matheus Cunha was on the end of Patrick Dorgu's cross to give United a 27th minute lead

Lisandro Martinez pounced to score from close range and complete the scoring at Old Trafford

The Sabah players were out on the grass more than an hour before the start, their excitement clear for all to see as they filmed themselves and took pictures.

Once the action started, they seemed undaunted by the occasion and the pace of Kaheem Parris and dangerman Joy Lance Mickels kept United's defence on its toes.

Not surprisingly, though, it was Carrick's side who made the better chances including two early opportunities on the right side of the box for Cunha and Noussair Mazraoui.

Two Tielemans passes led to Bruno Fernandes narrowly failing to find Sesko in front of goal as Rahman Dashdamirov intercepted, and Bryan Mbeumo cutting in from the right to fire straight at goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov before United made the breakthrough in the 27th minute.

Sabah were over-committed when an attack broke down close to half-way and they were punished. Mbeumo seized on the loose ball and it went through Sesko and Fernandes before Dorgu's first-time cross picked out Cunha whose close-range finish found its way past Pokatilov.

The man who couldn't score through the middle hadn't taken long to profit in his preferred position on the left side of United's attack.

While the lead was only one, Sabah were always in with a chance. They got closer to Senne Lammens' goal on occasions than Carrick would have liked, not least when Mickels headed into the side-netting from Parris' cross to the far post.

But United effectively killed the game off with two goals in the space of three minutes before half-time.

The first of them was created by Tielemans who started the move and then continued his run into the box to receive Cunha's pass, spinning cleverly to set up Fernandes for a clinical first-time finish.

Then the United captain broke from halfway and fed Mbeumo who slid a pass into the path of Sesko who rounded Pokatilov to score.

With the game all but won, you couldn't blame Carrick for taking off Tielemans at half-time to protect the Belgian ahead of the City game on Sunday. Mainoo and Sesko soon followed, and the changes continued after United made it 4-0 in the 68th minute.

Pokatilov fumbled a close-range effort from substitute Joshua Zirkzee, and Lisandro Martinez pounced to score from close range.

Credit to Sabah, they kept going and Mickels flashed a shot wide before Orphe Mbina headed against the bar in added time.

But having embarrassingly gone out at the group stage in 2023, United's first venture into the new league phase has gone smoothly.

Now it's onto the Metropolitano, which will host the Champions League final in June. It's far too early to say if United have even the slightest chance of being there, and games like this won't give us a clue either way.

Sports.title: Man City star Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend 'hit, bound and threatened with a knife by robbers while sleeping in their Paris flat'
Sports.content:
Man City star Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend 'hit, bound and threatened with a knife by robbers while sleeping in their Paris flat'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gianluigi Donnarumma and his then-pregnant girlfriend suffered a terrifying break-in in Paris in 2023, a court was told.

The Man City goalkeeper and Alessia Elefante, whom he has since married and had a child with, were hit, bound and threatened with a knife after robbers broke into their flat.

The incident took place in Avenue Montaigne, one of Paris' most famous and luxurious streets, with Donnarumma and his partner asleep at the time.

The keeper, 27, was then at PSG, and a Paris criminal court is currently conducting a two-day hearing about the ordeal.

Donnarumma is not expected to give evidence but a witness statement from him shed further light on what went on.

Court documents revealed how Donnarumma was woken by a man saying 'shh', before he was hit in the face with a knuckle duster and threatened with a knife.

Gianluigi Donnarumma and his then-pregnant girlfriend Alessia Elefante were hit, bound and threatened with a knife by robbers in their Paris flat in 2023 (pictured together in 2024)

The thieves left with keys to supercars, cash, watches and luxury handbags after robbing Donnarumma and Elefante (pictured in 2024)

The man then said: 'The watches, the watches'.

As per court documents, Donnarumma replied: 'I showed him the one on the dressing table, an Audemars Piguet.' Those watches can have a value worth up to hundreds of thousands of euros.

His partner told investigators that she was also woken up by the thieves who attacked her and shouted: 'The money, the watches.'

She subsequently gave them a Cartier watch, jewellery and €2,000 (£1718) in cash.

Elefante was then accosted for the code to a safe. However, she revealed she didn't know it and said it was empty anyway.

'They got angry thinking that I was lying,' she told investigators. 'They pulled me by the hair and one of them hit me on the thighs. I said I was pregnant but they continued.'

Donnarumma did then give them the code to the safe, but as Elefante had warned, there was nothing in there.

The court was told that the robbers left with keys to a Mercedes and a Lamborghini, cash, watches and luxury handbags.

Police also added that the four robbers managed to get into the flat by using a ladder to climb onto the roof, before they lowered themselves onto the balcony and broke in through windows.

Two individuals that are already in prison - Ilyas Kherbouch, a 21-year-old with at least 11 criminal convictions, and Khyan Mamouni - are accused of masterminding and ordering the robbery from their cells. They both deny the charges.

Kherbouch, who escaped from jail in March and spent 13 days on the run, caused a stir at the opening of the trial.

This came when he insulted and threatened police officers when they told his brother to leave the court.

'Come here, you,' he told them. 'What are you going to do?'

When warned that he could be expelled from the courtroom, he replied: 'I couldn’t care less. I don’t want to be present at the trial. I don’t give a s***.'

Donnarumma, now 27 and at Man City, was playing for PSG at the time of the terrifying ordeal

Two of the robbers, who were under the age of 18 when the incident happened, have already been given jail sentences of three and four years respectively at a children's court.

Another defendant Moktar Diop, 24, admitted to taking part but is not accused of resorting to violence, while a fourth suspect died by suicide in 2024. He had previously admitted to being involved but told investigators he had come under pressure from his accomplices.

Donnarumma and his partner's lawyers said previously that they were 'still profoundly shocked'.

The trial continues.

Sports.title: Pakistan endure another day of despair as miserable tour continues: This once great cricketing nation has been reduced to chaos and cluelessness as England close in on series whitewash, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Pakistan endure another day of despair as miserable tour continues: This once great cricketing nation has been reduced to chaos and cluelessness as England close in on series whitewash, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Moments after Ollie Robinson, immovable from the crest of his wave, had Saim Ayub caught in the slips by Harry Brook from the first ball of Pakistan’s second innings, a PA announcement warned Edgbaston stewards of a ‘Code Red’.

It had apparently been triggered by a fire alarm and, for a few seconds, the crowd fell eerily silent. But they burst into life three balls later when Robinson had Abdullah Shafique poking low to Joe Root at first slip, leaving the tourists nought for two and facing a Code Red situation of their own.

The fire alarm proved false, and Pakistan saved at least a little face by reaching 52 for two before rain ended play shortly after 5pm.

But as Root’s team closed in on a 3–0 whitewash in gloomy Birmingham, it was possible to feel two emotions at the same time: delight for England, who batted with panache and bowled with precision, and despair for Pakistan, a once great side reduced to chaos and cluelessness by the machinations of their board and the misery of their players.

There was uproar in Karachi and Lahore when, only two days into this series, their side were described as the worst their country had sent to these shores for 50 years. Those voices have fallen silent now, with England – in disarray themselves not long ago – largely doing as they pleased on the second day of this third and final Test.

Resuming on 156 for four, they thrashed 297 in 60 overs before being dismissed for 453, at which point Robinson took his series haul to 21 wickets at an average of 6.66 with the kind of precision that turns metronomes green with envy. It has all been closer to bloodsport than sport.

Ollie Robinson shone again as England closed in on a series whitewash over Pakistan

It was another day of despair for Pakistan as their miserable tour of England nears an end

We should be careful what we wish for, of course. Until recently, the idea of England winning every Test of a series would have been greeted with a snort of derision. But while they deserve credit for keeping their foot on Pakistan’s throat, the one-sidedness of the cricket has raised more questions about a format that rarely stops fretting over its future.

It’s no good grumbling about the unfettered growth of the T20 franchise circuit when Test cricket is properly contested by only a handful of nations. And it’s no good wondering why this inequality has been allowed to arise when the bigger nations shrug their shoulders at the ICC’s lopsided financial model, and the ICC themselves turn a blind eye to the game’s growing politicisation.

As this tour has confirmed, Pakistan are on the wrong side of each of these debates, with the chairman of their cricket board, Mohsin Naqvi, doubling up as the country’s interior minister, and presiding over the farcical culling of almost half their squad between Lord’s and Edgbaston.

It all meant the day proceeded along predictable lines, with Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence sniffing out any prospect of a Pakistani comeback by taking 73 from the morning’s first 10 overs while barely breaking sweat.

But if there has been one criticism of England, it has been the failure of their batsmen to convert starts into something more meaningful, and here again they promised more than they delivered.

Brook had struck the perfect tempo in moving to 75 in three and a quarter hours when he pushed an off-break from Ayub towards midwicket and set off for a single even as Shan Masood swooped on the ball, before running him out comfortably at the non-striker’s end.

Might Lawrence reach three figures instead? Moments before lunch, he contrived to chop a widish delivery from Mohammad Imran on to his stumps, and walked off in anguish for 65. Three half-centuries in four innings since his recall have been a good return, but the battle for top-six places is cranking up. This was an opportunity missed.

Jamie Smith, batting with a dislocated left index finger sustained in the field on the first day, played some meaty strokes for his third sixty in five innings, only to provide a simple return catch off a leading edge to Razaullah.

And while Robinson hit out for his second Test fifty, his dismissal left England with 21 half-centuries from six games this summer, and a lone hundred, by Ben Duckett against New Zealand at Trent Bridge.

Unless one of Pakistan’s batsmen can go big tomorrow, this will be the first Test series in England of three matches or more not to feature an individual century since the 1888 Ashes.

Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence were two of five England batsmen to pass 50 in their innings

This Pakistan side are one of the worst touring teams to ever come to here for a Test series

Not that any of this troubled Robinson as he performed his now customary demolition of Pakistan’s top order.

Ayub’s most recent cricket had been for Jamaica Kingsmen in the Caribbean Premier League, which most sensible set-ups might think was no kind of preparation for red-ball cricket under grey English skies. Sure enough, he completed a pair by wafting hopelessly at his first ball.

Cox, keeping in place of the injured Smith, now came up to the stumps for Shafique, who poked at Robinson as if in a trance. Since making 61 at Headingley, Shafique has managed 23 in five innings, and been dismissed in five of his six by Robinson.

Duckett put down a slip catch for the third time in the game when Shan Masood flashed at the luckless Gus Atkinson, while Jofra Archer lacked his usual menace. But such is the gulf between the sides that England can afford these blemishes and still win this game at a canter.

Sports.title: Dan Lawrence says Ollie Robinson is 'at the peak of his powers' after England bowler continues remarkable series against Pakistan - and gives verdict on own position in team
Sports.content:
Ollie Robinson is operating at the ‘peak of his powers’ and making his England team-mates believe he will take a wicket every ball.

That was the assessment from the slip cordon of Dan Lawrence, after Robinson struck twice in the opening over of Pakistan’s second innings at Edgbaston.

‘When he's bowling, when he's putting it in the same spot pretty much every ball, you certainly do feel in the game behind the stumps, especially when you've got someone pretty much at the peak of his powers,’ said Lawrence.

Robinson’s double strike took his series wickets tally to an astonishing 21 at a cost of just 6.66 runs each.

Bad weather ended play prematurely, leaving a Pakistan team yet to make 200 in five previous innings on 52 for two and requiring 268 more runs to make Joe Root’s England bat again.

At the other end of the day, Surrey’s Lawrence dominated the early scoring in a rapid start alongside Harry Brook, but like his fifth-wicket partner failed to turn a half century into a hundred, finishing with 65 off 82 balls, in a score of 453.

Dan Lawrence heaped praise on Ollie Robinson after he continued his remarkable series

Lawrence, who earlier scored 65, said the England bowler was 'at the peak of his powers'

With three 50s in four innings, the 29-year-old might have done enough to maintain his place in the squad for the winter tour of South Africa. Jacob Bethell will be back from knee surgery by then and Sam Curran has been nominated as Ben Stokes’ successor in the all-rounder role. The rest will be determined over the next fortnight.

Incoming coach Stephen Fleming is scheduled to arrive next week and is understood to be keen on getting around the country, talking to directors of cricket and coaches about the country’s leading players.

‘In regards to position in the team, only the selectors and the captain will know that, and I'm pretty happy with how I've contributed and we'll see what happens,’ Lawrence said.

‘I felt like I was playing really nicely and it was a really good surface to bat on against a tiring attack. I thought I was going to make a really big score to be honest, but it wasn't meant to be.’

Surrey team-mate Jamie Smith and Robinson also made half centuries, although the former was unable to take his place behind the stumps due to a dislocated finger.

Jordan Cox will keep wicket for the remainder of a contest that appears destined to finish on Friday, marking the beginning of the post-Bazball era with a 3-0 whitewash.

Sports.title: Six Nations matches in the USA! World Rugby say they want to host flagship games across the pond
Sports.content:
Six Nations matches in the USA! World Rugby say they want to host flagship games across the pond

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Rugby are pushing for the Six Nations to stage a money-spinning Test in America.

A sell-out crowd is expected for Saturday's clash between South Africa and New Zealand in Baltimore as the sport tries to open new markets.

The USA will host the 2031 World Cup and the sport's governing body believe there is enough appetite to stage a Stateside Six Nations fixture.

'In terms of the match-day economics, South Africa vs New Zealand is like a Six Nations match,' said World Rugby CEO Alan Gilpin.

'If you could take a Six Nations game to the right place, to a Boston or to a New York, where there's a lot of those fanbases, you can definitely drive the economics,

'I've used the example before… only as an example… of an Italy vs Ireland game. You've got two fantastic fan bases in the US of Irish and Italian fans.

World Rugby are pushing for the Six Nations to stage a money-spinning Test in America

'Now, you're going to have Irish fans and Italian fans in those respective home countries saying, "Hang on a minute, you know, we want to see our country play?"

'The counter argument to that [is] it's still Irish and Italian fans getting the chance to watch their team, so they're just not the ones who live in Ireland and Italy on this occasion. But that's a balancing piece we've got to work through.'

Sports.title: Baseball icon and Hiroshima atomic bomb survivor Isao Harimoto dies aged 86
Sports.content:
Baseball legend Isao Harimoto, who survived the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, has died aged 86.

The Korean-Japanese icon, who was born in Hiroshima in 1940 to Korean parents who migrated to Japan during the country's rule of Korea, died in Tokyo on Wednesday.

Growing up, he overcame huge adversity as a child. Firstly he was involved in an accident in 1944 that left him with severe burns on his right hand.

The result of that left him with limited mobility in his thumb and forefinger, while his middle three fingers became permanently curled.

Then a year later, he survived the United States of America's atomic bombing of Hiroshima during World War II on August 6, 1945.

Harimoto, whose birth name was Jang Hun, survived after his mother used her body to shield him and one of his sisters from the blast. However, sadly another sister did not survive. Between 60,000 and 80,000 people were killed instantly - with the final death toll calculated at 135,000.

Korean-Japanese baseball legend Isao Harimoto died aged 86 in Tokyo on Wednesday

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085

After a difficult childhood, Harimoto later turned his attention to baseball. He had to learn to play left-handed due to his injuries and wore a custom glove to fit his injured right hand that allowed him to catch the ball.

But despite those hindrances, Harimoto enjoyed a distinguished 23-year career - playing for Toei Flyers, the Yomiuri Giants and the Lotte Orions across his homeland. At the Flyers he helped them win their first Japan Series in 1962.

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085 and is the only player in Nippon Professional Baseball League (NPB) to surpass the 3,000 landmark.

Furthermore he is the only player in NPB history to hit over 500 home runs and steal more than 300 bases - with his figures at 504 and 319 respectively. By comparison, only three players in Major League Baseball history have achieved the same feat in Barry Bonds, Willie Mays and Alex Rodriguez.

An 18-time All-Star, he was inducted into the Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame in 1990.

The Golden Players Club, one of Japan’s two halls of fame, wrote: 'All members of the Meikyukai express our deep respect and gratitude for Mr Isao Harimoto’s many years of great achievements, and we sincerely pray [following] his passing.'

Sports.title: West Ham star threatens legal action over 'false allegations' after kidnap claims
Sports.content:
West Ham star threatens legal action over 'false allegations' after kidnap claims

West Ham United player Edson Alvarez is the subject of kidnapping claims, which he denies, and he is now threatening legal action over these 'false allegations'

View 2 Images Edson Alvarez has played just once for West Ham United this season (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

West Ham United player Edson Alvarez has broken his silence over allegations linking him to a kidnapping. The Mexico captain categorically rejects the claims and is threatening legal action against what he describes as false allegations.

‌



Alvarez, 28, is being connected to the alleged kidnapping of Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez, who claims to have produced a documentary about the player's career on his behalf. It is said to have cost over £150,000 (3.5 million pesos), which is apparently still outstanding.

‌



The producer has spoken to Mexican entertainment magazine TVNotas. Ordonez claims he was kidnapped two years ago after demanding payment.

‌



Baffled Champions League star learns his manager resigned straight after final whistle READ MORE :

Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision READ MORE :

In an obscure statement posted in both English and Spanish on his Instagram account, Alvarez says: "In light of the publications and statements that have circulated recently, I believe it is necessary to address this matter clearly and firmly. I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me.

"Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me.

"Until now, I had chosen not to respond. However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line.

‌



View 2 Images Edson Alvarez captained Mexico at the World Cup (Image: Jam Media, Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"If anyone believes they have evidence of any wrongdoing on my part, there are authorities, prosecutors, and courts before which they can present it. Serious accusations must be supported by evidence and presented before the appropriate authorities, not through statements in media outlets whose content prioritises sensationalism and media exposure over accuracy and truth.

‌



"I will not allow my name to be used to fuel conflicts between third parties or to gain media exposure. Therefore, given the seriousness of the statements that have been made, I have instructed my legal team to evaluate and pursue the appropriate legal action against any person who makes or disseminates false allegations against me.

"I also want to be clear regarding the publications that have attempted to connect me to this matter through my former partner's father: It is not my place to confirm, deny, or comment on what may be said about third parties, but it is my responsibility to make one thing absolutely clear: I have nothing to do with the events being reported.

Sports.title: Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision
Sports.content:
Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision

Mason Greenwood's manager at Fenerbahce resigned hours after a decision on the Manchester United academy graduate ahead of their first Champions League match for 18 years

View 2 Images Mason Greenwood's Fenerbahce manager has resigned only two months after signing the Manchester United academy graduate (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Fenerbahce manager Ismail Kartal announced his resignation during a press conference after their 1-1 draw with Roma in the Champions League. His fourth stint in charge of the Turkish giants ends days after reports that he was giving consideration to playing Mason Greenwood as a second forward.

Marco Asenio's lack of fitness and Matteo Guendouzi being suspended forced Kartal to think outside of the box. However, he ultimately decided against moving the Manchester United academy graduate from the right wing.

Greenwood, 24, assisted their equalising goal, which Archie Brown scored. However, the hosts were ultimately unable to find a winner.

Fenerbahce issue Mason Greenwood statement as UEFA investigate ex-Man Utd star READ MORE :

Man Utd receive explanation from Barcelona for Marcus Rashford transfer snub READ MORE :

In his press conference, Kartal said: "As of this evening, I would like to congratulate my players and announce my resignation from my post." He continued: "I have taken this decision to pave the way for my club.

"I have resigned from my post while there is still time, to assist my beloved Fenerbahce, my players and future managers. I wish everyone a good evening, on the understanding that I shall never return."

This resignation marks the end of his fourth spell in charge of the Turkish giants. He also spent a decade playing for them, winning the league twice.

View 2 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The former defender worked in Fenerbahce's academy for two years after retiring before beginning his managerial career elsewhere. Kartal returned as their assistant coach nine years later, winning two more titles and a pair of Turkish Cups.

After four years in that role, he took over as manager after the incumbent resigned. However, it took just a season before he decided to leave himself after finishing second to Galatasaray and being beaten by Buraspor in the cup semi-finals.

Kartal returned seven years later, replacing the future Nottingham Forest and Wolverhampton Wanderers head coach Vitor Pereira. He again led Fenerbahce to second place.

Kartal delivered a 99-point season; however, Galatasaray managed 102 to win the league, and he left. Then, two years later, Fenerbahce turned to him once again this summer.

However, despite coming through three rounds of Champions League qualifying to reach the tournament proper for the first time in 18 years, they lost their opening league match to Genclerbirligi, were beaten by Besiktas, and fell four points behind leaders Galatasaray.

Sports.title: New UK venue emerges to host Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight
Sports.content:
New UK venue emerges to host Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight

The all-British clash between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury could take place at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, rather than New York's Madison Square Garden, in November

View 2 Images Tyson Fury is due to fight Anthony Joshua (Image: Tyson Fury/Instagram)

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury could now settle their bitter feud in Wales.

‌



The British heavyweights were expected to clash at Madison Square Garden in New York on November 20. But Joshua’s contract includes a clause insisting the fight takes place in the UK and he has demanded that be honoured.

‌



Talks with Wembley reopened last week but Cardiff’s Principality Stadium is now in the running. The 80,000-seater stadium has the advantage of having a retractable roof.

‌



The showdown would be held in the early hours to suit the American market and could be pushed back into December. And a Friday night date is still favoured to avoid a clash with the American football schedule.

Mike Tyson did not stutter when offering Conor Benn vs Ryan Garcia prediction READ MORE :

Tyson Fury claims Anthony Joshua fight is OFF and names his next opponent READ MORE :

Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh and broadcaster Netflix want the fight to take place in the United States. But Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn believes it should be staged on home soil, with the clause in Joshua's contract backing up his stance.

‌



The much-hyped heavyweight clash has been caught up in arguments over the location of the fight. Last week Hearn threatened legal action against TKO Group Holdings — the parent company of Dana White's UFC and Zuffa Boxing — for trying to 'lure' Joshua to the US.

Wembley's chances of hosting the bout were scuppered by Alalshikh's request for a 2am start time, with the national stadium's curfew only able to be extended to 1am. That thrust Cardiff back into contention, with the Principality Stadium bidding for the event in July.

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua wants the fight to take place in the UK (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

"We'd be delighted to host this fight," a spokesperson for Welsh Rugby Union, which own the stadium, told Sky Sports at the time. "We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location."

The stadium hosted Joshua's win over Carlos Takam back in 2017 with 78,000 fans watching on, while AJ also fought Joseph Parker a year later in the same venue.

While best known for hosting rugby, the Principality Stadium has a rich boxing history, having seen Welshman Joe Calzaghe take on Mikkel Kessler in 2007. The Welsh capital was also the city which played host to Lennox Lewis vs Frank Bruno at the old National Stadium in 1993.

Sports.title: Benjamin Sesko sends clear message to Michael Carrick on night of few revelations for Man Utd
Sports.content:
Benjamin Sesko sends clear message to Michael Carrick on night of few revelations for Man Utd

Manchester United made light work for Azerbaijani side Sabah on their return to the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko sending a reminder to Michael Carrick with a well-taken goal

View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko took his goal well (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

When Benjamin Sesko was sent clear by Byran Mbeumo’s pass just before half-time, it never crossed his mind to fall under the rash challenge of goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov.

‌



He took the contact, did all he could to stay upright and rewarded himself with a routine finish. It is what natural-born central strikers do.

‌



From a formality of a night against hapless opponents, Michael Carrick learnt little of significance. But he was reminded that Sesko is a line-leader, an identikit number nine, even though he does not have it on his back.

‌



The Slovenian attacker has yet to start a Premier League match this season but will surely become the regular spearhead of this attack. And not just on the evidence of a good game against a team that will give target practice to everyone they meet in this phase of the Champions League.

Sesko scored a classic centre-forward’s goal when he came on as a late substitute and has been clinical for this United side since Carrick took over. And every angry-looking celebration tells you that he believes he should be starting every game.

It will be interesting to see if Carrick goes with him against Manchester City. And as soon as Sesko had hit United’s third of the night, the manager’s thoughts must have drifted towards Sunday’s challenge against Manchester City. Because this turned out to be as easy a task as everyone expected.

The nature of the game - a comfortable 4-0 win - gave Carrick the chance to try a new defensive combination but different personnel did not completely erase familiar failings.

‌



View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko waltzed around the Sabah goalkeeper to score (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

The failings were never going to be costly against an extremely limited attacking unit but there was still a distinct lack of assurance on the rare occasions the champions of Azerbaijan threatened to cause an offensive problem.

You would certainly expect to see Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot return to the starting line-up for the Manchester derby. And if he is fit, Luke Shaw - allowed to have a night off after what must have been a particularly severe case of cramp against Everton - will probably return to the side.

‌



In attacking mode, Patrick Dorgu was decent - setting up the opening goal for Matheus Cunha - but defensively, he was not convincing. He was exposed a couple of times, not least when Joy-Lance Mickels somehow failed to head home a sitter that would have levelled the score.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick rotated his team for the Sabah game (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Predictably, regret for Mickels and Sabah arrived fairly instantly, Bruno Fernandes applying side-footed justice to a nice Youri Tielemans assist. And after Sesko’s copybook finish, any pretence that it could be a meaningful contest had to be shelved.

‌



It was then just a case of how ruthless United would be in the second half. Sesko was withdrawn just after the hour mark - which might augur well for his chances of making Sunday's starting line-up - and it was over to Joshua Zirkzee to have a crack up top. And Zirkzee was involved in a comedy fourth for United that was eventually claimed by Lisandro Martinez.

That was the signal for Carrick to give an outing to youngsters Harry Amass and Shea Lacey and they enjoyed a nice 20 minutes in the Champions League limelight.

It was a pleasant end to a pleasant, if bloodless, return to the grand European stage.
