World.title: Iraq secures US, South Korean, Turkish air defenses
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNew.com) — Iraq has finalized contracts for new air defense systems from the United States, South Korea, and Turkey, with the first deliveries due shortly as Baghdad prepares to regain more control of its airspace when the US-led coalition mission expires on September 30.

Baghdad intends to deploy the technology around the nation to safeguard oil installations, important infrastructure, and Iraqi territory while it develops an integrated network of long-, medium-, and short-range defenses backed by radar and command systems.

The effort took on new significance as Iraq’s airspace became a conduit for missiles, drones, and military aircraft amid regional warfare involving Iran, the US, and Israel.

Iran has also directly attacked US sites in Iraq, highlighting Baghdad’s inadequate capacity to prevent foreign assaults and protect its airspace on its own.

Iraq had initially planned a six-year program to upgrade its air defenses, but Al-Zaidi reduced the timeline to three years.

The increase corresponds with the final evacuation of soldiers assigned to the multinational coalition’s mission in Iraq.

Baghdad claims Iraqi troops can now manage the residual ISIS threat, and Operation Inherent Resolve will officially finish inside Iraq at the end of the month.

The new systems from the United States, South Korea, and Turkey are likely to play a key role in Iraq’s efforts to bridge a long-standing air-defense gap and gain more control over its skies after the coalition departs.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis seize key city on Red Sea: military source
World.content:
Sanaa – Yemen’s Houthis seized control of the strategic Red Sea port city of Mokha on Thursday, a Yemeni military source told AFP, as the Iran-backed group reported fresh strikes by Saudi forces.

The Houthis, who control large parts of northwest Yemen, launched a large-scale offensive last week against Yemeni government forces, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.

They also launched attacks on Saudi territory that left dozens of people wounded, in a conflict that has reignited during the Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

Witnesses told AFP they saw Houthi forces entering Mokha on Thursday while chanting “death to America, death to Israel”.

The Yemeni military source said they were advancing towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait “after having taken control of Mokha”.

The waterway, which links Asia to Europe via the Red Sea and Suez Canal, has gained importance as a transit route since the start of the wider Middle East war, which saw Iran blockade the Strait of Hormuz.

The military source said the Houthis also seized Zuqar Island, in the southern Red Sea, “after rocket attacks and a ground assault carried out using boats transporting fighters”.

Also on Thursday, the Houthis reported airstrikes.

“The Saudi enemy’s air force conducted around 40 strikes in recent hours in the governorates of Taiz, Hodeida, Al-Jawf and Marib,” Houthi news agency Saba said.

– Hundreds dead –

Yemen relapsed into war in July after years of relative calm punctured by sporadic violence and deepening poverty.

Since last week, the fighting in Yemen has left more than 500 dead, mostly combatants, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources.

It has also forced nearly 20,000 people to flee their homes, the International Organization for Migration said on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition battling the Houthis said the anti-government fighters fired ballistic missiles and drones at several cities in southern Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi civil defence issued alerts warning of “potential danger” in two areas, Khamis Mushait and Abha, before lifting them soon after.

The Houthis triggered the return to hostilities in July when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.

The government retaliated by striking Sanaa airport, an attack the Houthis blamed on its sponsor, Saudi Arabia.

The ongoing exchanges risk returning Yemen to a conflict that left hundreds of thousands of people dead and sparked one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

The Houthis, after seizing Yemen’s capital and forcing out the internationally recognised government, fought a Saudi-led coalition from 2015 until a United Nations-brokered ceasefire in 2022.

World.title: France will not support Infantino in FIFA election: federation chief
World.content:
Paris – France will not support the candidacy of Gianni Infantino, who is running for a new term as FIFA president in March 2027, the French Football Federation (FFF) announced on Thursday.

The FFF is aligning itself with the position of other European federations such as Belgium, Italy, Scotland, Sweden and Wales, who have also publicly withdrawn support for Infantino.

FIFA confirmed last weekend that Infantino will stand in the FIFA presidential election next March, despite the backlash over his now-abandoned plan to bring private investment into the men’s and women’s World Cups.

At this stage, the 56-year-old Swiss is the only candidate.

“We believe that the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us,” FFF president Philippe Diallo said in a statement.

“That is why, by a unanimous decision of its members, the French Football Federation has decided to withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the FIFA presidency.”

World.title: Vance takes spotlight as Republicans close Trump-heavy convention
World.content:
Dallas – US Republicans return to the stage Thursday to close their midterm convention, still betting that Donald Trump’s political magnetism can overcome grim election forecasts — while giving Vice President JD Vance a prime-time showcase as a potential heir.

Trump will dominate the finale of the two-day gathering, delivering closing remarks after Vance’s keynote address at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas.

The unusual convention has been built around a simple message: Trump may not literally be on November’s ballot, but Republicans want the president’s supporters to behave as though he is.

That strategy comes with the party under heavy pressure.

US election tracking site Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats will win the House 230-205 and take the Senate 51-49. Trump’s approval rating has languished in the low-to-mid 30s amid stubborn inflation and an unpopular war with Iran.

Trump dramatically raised the stakes in his opening night keynote Wednesday, promising a $5,000 “Trump dividend” to every American adult if Republicans retain both chambers of Congress in November.

He also made explicit the convention’s central electoral pitch.

“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot — I’m on the ballot, I’m on the ballot — just one more time,” he said.

He strongly defended the Iran war, predicting victory would bring down oil prices, and warned that the United States would become a “communist country” if Democrats prevail in the election.

– Heir apparent? –

Vance’s appearance adds intrigue to the closing night.

The 42-year-old vice president is widely regarded as an early front-runner for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, although he has said he will not make a decision until after the midterms.

His place immediately before Trump’s closing remarks gives him one of the most prominent speaking slots of the convention and an opportunity to address a party already beginning to consider its post-Trump future.

But in the more immediate contest, Republicans need Vance and other party figures to help deliver Trump’s voters in an election in which the president himself is absent from the ballot.

Republicans also hope to use the closing night to promote tax cuts, immigration enforcement and other administration policies while depicting Democrats as increasingly extreme.

The convention has resembled an extended Trump rally more than a traditional party meeting, with no nominations or formal business and more than 50 speakers or presentations each night.

The atmosphere inside the arena on Wednesday was festive despite the political headwinds. Yet not all Republicans have embraced the experiment.

Numerous lawmakers in competitive races chose to remain in their districts rather than spend valuable campaign time in Dallas, while both convention nights were facing competition from the opening games of the NFL season.

Those who have shown up will be looking for evidence that Vance can emulate Trump in energizing the voters who powered the flamboyant billionaire’s return to the White House.

And Vance, whether he acknowledges it or not, will be speaking to a party already asking who might inherit those voters when Trump is no longer the headline act.

“If the American people give Republicans another chance to govern, we’re going to create more prosperity,” Vance told Fox News after Trump’s speech.

“And we want the American people to share in that prosperity.”

World.title: Iraqi Airways doubles Baghdad-Amman flights on peak days
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Airways will double flights between Baghdad and Amman on peak travel days beginning Friday, Sept. 11, in response to increased passenger demand between Iraq and Jordan.

The airline said that it would boost flights from one to two each day on Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays, increasing capacity on three of the busiest days of the week.

Daily service will continue on the other days.

The increased schedule provides additional alternatives for travelers traveling between Baghdad International Airport and Amman’s Queen Alia International Airport, both of which are already available on Iraqi Airways’ booking network.

Iraqi Airways said that the extra flights are being added in response to a large increase in passenger traffic on the route, with the goal of providing more flexibility as demand develops.

The move improves air connectivity between Iraq and Jordan, which have strong business, tourist, and family travel relations.

The development coincides with Iraqi Airways’ efforts to expand fleet operating capacity and widen its regional and international network.

As part of its attempts to increase fleet availability, the state-owned airline has recently resumed aircraft operations and expanded repair capabilities.

The revised Baghdad-Amman timetable becomes effective on September 11.

World.title: Seahawks beat Patriots again in NFL opener
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Seattle Seahawks shrugged off Sam Darnold’s early injury to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the NFL’s opening game, piling more misery on the team they defeated in last season’s Super Bowl.

Backup quarterback Drew Lock threw for 187 yards and a touchdown to Jackson Smith-Njigba, as reigning champs Seattle rallied from 10-0 down for their 11th consecutive win.

The latest loss inflicted more pain on New England quarterback Drake Maye, who threw three costly interceptions, including a particularly wasteful one in the final seconds from field-goal range to throw away a patchy, defensive game.

Maye — who had been sacked six times in February’s Super Bowl, and suffered three more here — was picked off by Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe in the end zone.

“It was game on the line. You know, fourth quarter… we only was up three points, and we got to take the ball away, and we did,” said Jobe.

“Holy cow, we did it! Here we are, one-and-zero,” said Lock.

And it was a night to forget for the Patriot’s new acquisitions too, as AJ Brown limped off with an ankle injury and Romeo Doubs was beaten for one interception and was guilty of a terrible drop shortly before a second.

The Seattle evening began in festive fashion. A new Super Bowl LX championship banner was unfurled from Lumen Field’s colossal rafters. Pearl Jam’s Mike McCready performed the national anthem.

But the mood was punctured on the game’s first drive. Darnold was sacked on third down by Dre’Mont Jones, and limped to the locker room via the medical tent clutching his hip. He did not return.

The Patriots struck first. Maye hurled the ball 34 yards to Brown on the edge of the endzone. Defensive pass interference was called, and Maye immediately lofted a short pass over the top to newly drafted tight end Eli Raridon for the season’s first touchdown.

Seattle fought back. Veteran receiver Cooper Kupp took a stunning one-handed diving catch from Lock for a 24-yard gain on third down. The pair then celebrated a touchdown pass, before the score was ruled out for an illegal shift, and the Seahawks settled for a field goal.

– Interceptions –

After a promising Patriots drive, Maye’s ambitious downfield hurl to Romeo Doubs ricocheted off Rodney Thomas’s fingers to Nehemiah Pritchett for the game’s first interception.

The Seahawks made Maye pay. At 4th & 1, Lock passed to an open Smith-Njigba, who raced past the Patriots defense at lightning speed for a 45-yard touchdown, tying the game 10-10.

Seattle drove again, with Lock peppering passes before charging 14 yards into the red zone. A series of errors from a hugely promising position meant it was only a field goal.

An increasingly desperate Maye suffered his first sack of the night trying to break through the Seattle defense. Two more swiftly followed, though the Patriots somehow edged the ball upfield, twice successfully going for fourth downs.

But sensing a chance for a winning touchdown, despite being in field goal range, Maye hurled a deep right pass to Mack Hollins in the end zone, resulting in Jobe’s game-ending interception.

“We’ve moved on. This is a new season. We did the banner thing. It’s time to find out who 2026 Seahawks are going to be,” said Lock.

World.title: Philippine ferry fire kills 5, dozens missing
World.content:
Manila – At least five people were killed and 86 remain missing after a fire erupted aboard a ferry near a tourist hotspot in the Philippine province of Palawan, the coast guard said Thursday.

The blaze broke out on the M/V June Aster Wednesday evening about 2.2 kilometres (1.3 miles) offshore, the coast guard said, adding that five casualties had been brought ashore.

Video shared by the coast guard on Facebook showed the vessel completely engulfed in flames.

Hundreds of people, desperate for news about the incident, have left comments on the Coron town mayor’s Facebook page, searching for relatives, friends and even a dog.

“Based on the data we have right now on rescued (42) and the casualties, we still have 87 people who are unaccounted for,” coast guard Captain Noemi Cayabyab told a local radio station on Thursday.

The ship’s manifest had listed 134 passengers and crew, Cayabyab said.

Of those rescued, 38 were passengers and four were crew, she added.

Hours later, the Philippine Coast Guard told reporters that another person had been rescued, but their identity had yet to be confirmed.

“Just to make it clear, this is live data and may change as our search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Cayabyab said in the radio interview.

“However, we have not yet been able to obtain information from the rescued individuals because we have not been able to speak with them,” she said, adding attempts to put out the blaze were ongoing.

There were no immediate reports of foreigners on board.

Tracking data from MarineTraffic showed the June Aster had departed from Manila.

In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people.

The M/V Trisha Kerstin 3 sank along nearly the same route where 31 people died in 2023 after a fire broke out aboard the Lady Mary Joy 3 ferry.

World.title: Asian Games begin with Qatar basketball win, nine days before opening ceremony
World.content:
Tokyo – The Asian Games began in Japan on Thursday when Qatar beat Iran in the men’s basketball opening group game, the first action in the continental multi-sport showpiece that has more participants than the Olympics.

Over 17,000 athletes and officials are expected to take part in 43 sports at the Nagoya-Aichi Games — which do not officially start until the opening ceremony on September 19 and will run until October 4.

Several events such as basketball, football, cricket, hockey and modern pentathlon will get under way before the opening ceremony.

Qatar held off a comeback from Iran to win their Group B encounter 59-35 at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya in the first match of a men’s basketball competition that will hold medal finals on September 20, the day after the opening ceremony.

Los Angeles 2028 Olympics qualifying spots are up for grabs in several sports at the Asian Games, which are returning to Japan for the first time since 1994.

Organisers hope the athletes will have a “unique experience” staying in eye-catching accommodation ranging from a cruise liner and wooden containers to standard hotel rooms.

Officials are confident that the plan will not be affected by Japan’s typhoon season, which is usually in full swing in September-October.

Weather has already caused disruptions, with record rainfall on Tuesday forcing hundreds of athletes briefly to evacuate their accommodation.

Rainwater also leaked into some competition venues, with more wet weather forecast for the coming days.

Among those in action at the Games will be Philippine tennis sensation Alexandra Eala and a pair of world-class teenage talents in 15-year-old Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi.

World.title: Retro looks, current jibes: Netas give '80s a new spin
World.content:
NEW DELHI: "The 80s called, I answered," quipped agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan as he posted on X a picture of him from that era. Congress Kerala posted an invented Gujarat street scene; BJP Telangana replied with a fabricated bar scene tagged "Lusiana, Italy", apparently alluding to Sonia Gandhi's birthplace.

The '80s came calling, and India's politicians answered with aviators, old albums and a little swagger. Then party accounts joined the nostalgia trip, remembering to pack a few jibes for the other side.

Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal shared an AI portrait of himself in a suit and aviators, saying: "Vibing to the 80s trend". Union ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal wrote: "80s vibes: Styles fade, but the appeal is forever!" A line fit for a campaign, vintage or otherwise.

Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma chimed in: "Back to the 80s eh!" Telangana CM Revanth Reddy appeared beside a motorbike in his post. For a while, the competition seemed to be over who wore the decade best.

Others let their albums do the talking. Congress neta Renuka Chowdhury offered a reality check: "Me? I've got receipts." She shared what she de-scribed as an '80s Savvy magazine cover featuring herself.

Union minister Kiren Rijiju followed his AI makeover with a throwback he said needed neither AI nor ChatGPT.





Congress MP Shashi Tharoor posted pictures with his sons, Ishaan and Kanishk. "I thought I'd join the trend the old-fashioned way," he wrote, a real photograph a boast of its own amid the trend built on imagining the past.

BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan shared wedding footage featuring then chief minister MGR and opposition leader M Karunanidhi. Rival camps on one guest list.

World.title: Global climate record: August this year joint-warmest month with July '23
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally across all calendar months, on a par with July 2023, said Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) of the European Union's space programme on Thursday.It noted that this Aug was 1.65Â° Celsius above the estimated pre-industrial (1850-1900) baseline, marking the first month above 1.5Â° Celsius since Nov 2025, and the period from June to Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest three-month period on record globally, on a par with 2024."Aug 2026 was a remarkable month in the global climate record. It was both the warmest Aug and the warmest month ever recorded," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Though the global average temperature rise in the month breached the limit of 1.5Â°C, it technically did not cross the Paris Agreement threshold, which actually refers to long-term temperature increase over decades, not over one to five years.Under the Paris Agreement, countries agreed to keep long-term global average surface temperature well below 2Â°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5Â°C by end of century.Nevertheless, the rise in temperatures to this level in Aug is a stark warning that the world is getting warmer, with its consequences of extreme weather events, glacier melt, sea-level rise and uneven distribution of rainfall over a short period of time being visible across the globe."Until humanity stops burning colossal amount of coal, oil and gas, the pollution this causes will keep baking our planet, and extreme heat will keep smashing all-time records, killing millions and costing trillions, hitting transport and health systems, and pushing up prices for household basics like food," said UN Climate Change executive secretary Simon Stiell in his response to the report.Aug in India was the warmest Aug in the country since 1901, with a mean monthly temperature of 28.01Â°C.

World.title: Last year's row in mind, govt says won't reduce med PG cut-off
World.content:
NEW DELHI: After facing severe backlash last year for reducing the cut-off percentile to zero for admission to medical colleges for super speciality courses, the Centre Thursday told Supreme Court that it has decided not to reduce cut-off marks this year, but the top court asked govt to take a fresh look and reconsider its decision.

Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe about govt's decision. She informed the court that the decision was arrived at after consultations between all stakeholders - ministry of health, medical counselling committee (MCC) and National Medical Commission (NMC).

"As per the directions of Supreme Court in the Kevin Joy case (2023), it has been decided to conduct a 'special stray round' by the medical counselling committee for the purpose of filling up the vacant super speciality seats arising out of NEET-SS 2025 counselling without reduction in the percentile criteria prescribed for admission in the said special stray round," Bhati said while placing before the court a one-page note on govt's decision.

Advocate Rashmi Nandakumar, appearing for some of the petitioners, however, told the bench that around 2,000 seats in colleges would remain vacant if the cut-off percentile was not reduced. She said the authorities have consistently adopted appropriate measures, including special rounds, mop-up rounds, stray vacancy rounds and relaxation of eligibility criteria, whenever substantial super speciality seats remained vacant to ensure optimum utilisation of available seats.





Taking note that a substantial number of seats would get wasted, the bench asked the Centre to reconsider its decision and brief the court on the next date of hearing. As the ASG urged the court to put it in its order, the bench passed a brief order on reconsideration of the decision. The petitioners pleaded that at least a mop-up/stray vacancy round be conducted for seats remaining vacant after completion of the ongoing counselling process so that no super speciality seat was allowed to go to waste.

With over 18,000 post-graduate medical seats across the country remaining vacant, the National Board of Examination in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) revised the qualifying percentile for NEET-PG 2025 admissions, reducing it to zero from the 40th percentile for reserved categories -- which enabled even those scoring as low as minus 40 out of 800 to take part in the third round of counselling for PG medical seats. According to the notice published by NBEMS, the NEET-PG cut-off for the general category was reduced to the seventh percentile from the 50th.

World.title: Russia President Vladimir Putin arrives in India ahead of Brics Summit 2026, to meet PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Russian President

arrived in India on early Friday ahead of the Brics Summit 2026.

Russian president's official air vehicle landed at Delhi airport.

During his visit, Putin is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister

and participate in a series of bilateral meetings.

This mark his first overseas participation in a

Summit since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.

The two leaders are expected to discuss the full range of India-Russia ties, with trade, energy and defence cooperation likely to figure prominently.

The visit comes just days after PM Modi and Putin met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek on August 31. At that meeting, the two leaders reviewed cooperation in areas including political ties, trade, defence, energy, space and mobility, while also discussing the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region.

Putinâs presence in Delhi also comes as India and Russia seek to deepen economic engagement despite mounting geopolitical pressure over Moscowâs war in Ukraine and Western restrictions on Russian trade.

Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov had earlier said the two sides are also exploring cooperation in rare earths, along with the possible sale of Sukhoi Su-57 stealth fighter jets to India.

It is scheduled. It is scheduled for Friday, so first, like always, they will touch on the bilateral agenda. Trade and economic cooperation is a very wide scope."

World.title: SC junks anti-HPV vax PIL, says plea has ulterior motive
World.content: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday dismissed a PIL by a doctors' association challenging India's nationwide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme for adolescent girls to protect them against cervical cancer and said it did not behove medical practitioners to take an anti-vaccine stance.Though the NGO's counsel clarified at the outset that the PIL was not against the vaccination programme but for putting in place mechanisms to take care of adverse reactions and compensation, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant said, "The PIL is definitely anti-vaccine." It gave the option to the lawyer to withdraw or invite adverse comments.When the counsel continued to argue for prior informed consent of parents of the target population of adolescent girls, the bench said the PIL appeared to have been filed with an ulterior motive and lacked bona fide. It said when there was an established mechanism for taking care of adverse reactions and compensation in individual cases, it did not behove doctors to oppose vaccination when World Health Organisation had recommended it.The NGO said eminent oncologists have pointed to data that shows cervical cancer incidence has declined over the past three decades.

World.title: Recent Brics summits didn't benefit India, says PC; BJP hits back
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP and Congress sparred ahead of the Brics summit as P Chidambaram questioned if its last few meetings have brought India any tangible benefits, comments slammed by Nitin Nabin as familiar whining by the opposition over the country's rise and growth.

"World is looking at India but comments being made by Congress members are shameful. Rahul Gandhi and Congress netas have been insulting India on foreign soil. Now when India is hosting a big international event, they are again pained," the BJP chief told reporters.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

These "naraz fufas", a barb PM Modi has used to dismiss criticism from Congress netas, were similarly hurt when India hosted G20 and AI summits, Nabin said.

His remarks came after Chidambaram told a news agency, "I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results. In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20 and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see.

In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, Brics summits resulted in tangible benefits."

BJP spokesman Sudhanshu Trivedi mocked Chidambaram, saying that when so many world leaders are coming to India for the summit, he seems to place his wisdom above theirs.

World.title: Amid West Asia conflict, Iran president to meet Modi today
World.content:
PM Modi to meet Iran prez

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For the first time in eight years, an Iranian president will visit India, with Masoud Pezeshkian set to arrive in New Delhi for the 18th Brics summit Friday, amid escalating West Asia tensions. Shortly after his arrival, Pezeshkian will participate in the Brics Business Forum meeting along with PM Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin before joining Modi for a bilateral.The last Iranian president to visit India was Hassan Rouhani in 2018. Iran has confirmed participation by the president in the Brics summit, while Saudi and the UAE - both parties to the West Asia conflict along with Tehran - will be represented by foreign minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud and Abu Dhabi crown prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.Pezeshkian is likely to reiterate his message before Modi for India to help end the war and address Tehran's concerns, including through a strong condemnation of "illegal aggression" against Iran, in the proposed Brics declaration. In meetings with Putin and Pezeshkian Friday, Modi is expected to stress the need for new members to subscribe to consensus in the grouping and work towards a unified joint declaration at the summit on key issues amid deepening divisions over West Asia.India agreed to the SCO Bishkek Declaration that condemned attacks on Iran. The declaration did not name the US or Israel though to prevent resistance from members that have cultivated ties with Washington.However, with the presence of UAE in Brics, balancing the interests of both sides has not been easy for India's Brics chairship. It's unlikely that the UAE will agree to an SCO-like formulation without seeking an condemnation of Iranian attacks.Gulf states the UAE and Saudi Arabia are only dialogue partners in SCO.India will prioritise the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection in the declaration. If the deadlock persists, govt will look to insulate economic agreements from the West Asia discord by acknowledging respective national positions.

World.title: Checks on e-commerce platforms from October: FSSAI
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: Having secured nearly 2,000 convictions in food safety cases across the country, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is now stepping up enforcement, including holding e-commerce platforms responsible for products sold through them and proposing stricter action against high-fat, sugar and salt (HFSS) foods near schools, its CEO Rajit Punhani said Thursday.FSSAI will begin checks on e-commerce platforms from next month. Platforms will have to carry out due diligence and ensure that products listed on them comply with food safety regulations."We are holding e-commerce platforms responsible. They cannot take this plea that they are just aggregators, they are just platforms. It is your responsibility, your due diligence," Punhani said.FSSAI has already held consultations with e-commerce companies. Punhani identified e-commerce and labelling as two major consumer-focused reforms expected over the next year.The regulator has also proposed restricting the sale of HFSS food within 50 metres of schools to protect children from unhealthy food. Punhani said the earlier challenge was the absence of a clear definition of HFSS food. The Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition, a govt nutrition research institute, has now provided criteria that FSSAI plans to use.On enforcement, Punhani said FSSAI had suspended licences, closed establishments and launched prosecutions. Around 600 people had been arrested in criminal cases involving unsafe food in the previous six months, he said. He cited around 1,900 convictions and 33,000 notices issued across India for food safety violations, including adulteration, mislabelling and substandard food.FSSAI is also tightening rules on food claims and marketing. It does not allow "100%" claims except in cases under litigation, while "pure" and "natural" can be used only for single-ingredient products, provided nothing has been added. The regulator has also written to Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade and the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks over the use of "healthy" as a trademark.Punhani said the term "energy drink" would not be allowed on labels as it could mislead consumers, with such products classified as caffeinated beverages, while the proposed red warning system would also cover aerated, carbonated and caffeinated beverages. The regulator has issued notices to six celebrities over misleading food-related endorsements, with three having responded.

World.title: Bihar Congress disciplinary committee issues show-cause notices to 29 leaders
World.content:
The Disciplinary Committee of the Bihar Pradesh Congress Committee on Thursday (September 10, 2026) has issued show-cause notices to 29 leaders on charges of anti-party activities and indiscipline.

The action follows their active participation in a protest held near the All India Congress Committee (AICC) headquarters in New Delhi on September 8, 2026, against the Bihar Pradesh Congress leadership.

Kapildev Prasad Yadav, Chairman of the Bihar Pradesh Congress Disciplinary Committee, stated in the notice that the involvement of the concerned leaders in the said activity violates party policy, discipline, and directives, and constitutes a serious act of indiscipline.

The notice directs all the concerned leaders to submit a written explanation to the Disciplinary Committee of the Bihar Pradesh Congress Committee within 72 hours of receiving the notice and to state why disciplinary action should not be taken against them.

The committee has clarified that if no explanation is received within the stipulated timeframe, or if the response provided is found to be unsatisfactory, the committee will be free to take unilateral disciplinary action against the concerned leaders in accordance with party rules.

Prominent among the 29 leaders, who were issued show-cause notices, are former MLAs Anil Singh and Poonam Devi, as well as Congress leaders Vidhushekhar Pandey, Bharat Bhushan Dubey, Satyendra Yadav, and Mrityunjay Singh.

A group of Bihar Congress leaders had staged a peaceful sit-in outside the party headquarters demanding removal of the Bihar unit in-charge Krishna Allavaru and State president Rajesh Kumar, holding them responsible for the party’s dismal performance in the state.

Reacting to the show-cause notice, Anand Madhab, AICC member, said that a peaceful protest by dedicated Congress members in Delhi was concluded and in-charge, AICC Headquarters Manish Chatrath, had come and assured all the protesters that their grievances would be heard.

“Yet, Krishna Allavaru and Rajesh Ram went ahead and issued notices to 29 leaders. This is a despicable act. We had gone to our own ‘home’—to our leadership—to present our demands; there was nothing wrong with that. If our grievance is against these very two leaders, where else would we go? We would naturally go to the High Command,”Mr. Madhab, who was also present during Delhi’s protest, said.

He added, “In reality, these two leaders seem to have taken a contract to finish Bihar Congress and its members, but they forget that dedicated Congress members are not afraid of this. Two things have become clear from the notices. First, that they are afraid; and second, that they have acknowledged that numerous former MLAs, former district presidents, and senior state leaders are against them.”

Mr. Madhab also argued that the authority to take action against an AICC member rests with the National President and the National Disciplinary Committee, not the state committee.

Earlier, on November 17, 2025, the disciplinary committee had issued a show-cause notice to 47 leaders for anti-party activities and making statements against the party line during the assembly election.

World.title: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrives in New Delhi to attend BRICS summit
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday (September 11, 2026) began a three-day visit to India to participate in the BRICS summit and meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi to expand bilateral trade, investment and energy cooperation.

Mr. Putin is accompanied by a high-level delegation.

It will be his first in-person participation at a BRICS summit outside Russia since the war in Ukraine began in February 2022.

The two-day BRICS summit hosted by India starting on Saturday (September 11, 2026) is expected to focus on boosting collective resilience in food, energy, health, disaster reduction and critical supply chains with New Delhi positioning the bloc as an effective anchor to navigate a fragmented geopolitical environment.

The summit in New Delhi is taking place against the backdrop of a global economy facing the adverse impacts of the Russia-Ukraine war, the West Asia crisis, especially the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the Trump administration’s trade and tariff policies.

Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Indonesian counterpart Prabowo Subianto, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung are among the top leaders attending the summit.

Mr. Putin and Mr. Modi are scheduled to hold wide-ranging bilateral talks on Friday afternoon.

The meeting is expected to focus on enhancing cooperation in a range of areas, including defence, energy, technology, pharmaceuticals and people-to-people exchanges.

World.title: Supreme Court declines pre-arrest relief to Abhishek Banerjee’s PA
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 10, 2026) refused anticipatory bail to Sumit Roy, personal assistant to TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee, in connection with the Salboni land grab case.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant decided to not interfere with a Calcutta High Court order of August denying him pre-arrest bail.

The West Bengal government, represented by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, argued that Mr. Roy’s answers were proving evasive and his custodial interrogation was necessary to the investigation.

The case was registered under penal provisions relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy.

Mr. Mehta alleged that about ₹15 crore was deposited by Mr. Roy in multiple transactions.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Mr. Roy, countered that there was not a single shred of proof of his client’s involvement in the case. He submitted that Mr. Roy had already undergone approximately 88 hours of questioning but had not been confronted with documents or witnesses directly linking him to the alleged transactions.

He argued that the investigating agency was trying to link the banking transactions of the TMC with the personal account of his client. Even the other accused had denied Mr. Roy’s involvement before the investigating agency. However, the court was not convinced.

World.title: Maratha protesters will head to Mumbai, says Jarange Patil
World.content:
“We are going to Mumbai, the date will be announced on September 12, once we all gathered at Antarwali Sarathi,” said Maratha Activist Manoj Jarange Patil as his indefinite hunger strike demanding reservation for the community entered 13th day on Thursday (September 10, 2026).

“We are not waiting for government’s delegation to visit his protest site, but waiting for supporters to assemble and then decide the next course of action,” said Mr. Jarange Patil.

Mr. Jarange Patil and his supporters are staging protest across the state demanding government to issue the certificates based on Kunbi entries in the Hyderabad and Satara Gazette records to eligible members of the Maratha community and validate the certificates, instead of cancelling them.

Mahayuti minister Uday Samant said,”We are taking every step to resolve the issue before September 12.” Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule highlighted that the government has installed the camps to facilitate the process of issuing the certificates. “The steps are carried to give reservation under OBC category based on the SOPs of government,” he added.

While speaking to media persons at Antarwali Sarati in Jalna district, he said, “We will watch whether the camps organised to issue Kunbi certificates is because of the ongoing agitation or to cancel the issued certificates.”

Soared relations with Mahayuti

A day ago, Mr. Jarange Patil accused Maratha quota sub-committee chairman Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil of betrayal to the community by being a sweet talker.

He criticised DCM Eknath Shinde and targeted Shiv Sena minister Sanjay Shirsat, saying, “In last three years, I have been respectfull towards Mr. Shinde but now he is speaking in favour of party. This is because of Shirsat, the relations have soared,” he added.

Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut targeted Mahayuti alliance, saying “The government wants to kill him. They used Manoj Jarange Patil for political gain.”

World.title: Gauhati High Court seeks clarity on rehab for evicted people in Assam
World.content:
The Gauhati High Court has sought clarity from the Assam government on providing rehabilitation and compensation for people displaced during an eviction drive in September 2024.

The Kamrup Metropolitan district authorities conducted the eviction drive at Kachutoli in the Sonapur area, about 20 km east of Guwahati, to clear 100 bighas of notified tribal land. The evicted were mostly migrant Bengali Muslims.

In an order on September 7, Justice Devashis Barua issued notices to various government departments to record their stands on the plea for rehabilitation and compensation by 76 petitioners through affidavits by October 6.

The petitioners represent some of the 650 families, comprising about 2,000 people, who were evicted from September 23 to 25, 2024, their advocate Zunaid Khalid said.

The court observed that the petitioners have been residing on private patta land (property whose ownership is officially recorded) after they were “evicted from their occupation” without receiving any rehabilitation or compensation.

The eviction at Kachutoli began on September 9, 2024. The displaced villagers reoccupied the land three days later, triggering tension.

The authorities resumed the demolition drive. The villagers protested, and two people—Haider Ali and Jubahir Ali—were killed in police firing, while 33 others, including government and police officials, were injured.

The local administration carried out the final eviction drive by September 25.

World.title: Four-day Kashmir film festival sharpens spotlight on filmmakers’ destination, local storytellers
World.content:
The four-day star-studded 1st International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) concluded on Thursday (September 10, 2026) in Srinagar and put a sharp spotlight on Kashmir as filmmakers’ destination and a platform for locals to emerge as storytellers.

Besides the screening of 120 movies from around 30 countries, scores of locals, including students, film enthusiasts, artists and filmmakers, were provided a platform to meet and learn from the big names of Bollywood like Ramesh Sippy, Vidhu Vinod Chopra, Imtiaz Ali etc.

Locals had masterclasses and interactive sessions on varies subjects related to cinema with filmmakers like Rahhat Shah Kazmi, Kapil Matoo, Munjal Shroff, Subbiah Nallamuthu, Arun Chadda, Yadu Vijaykrishnan, Supriyo Sen, Chittaranjan Tripathy etc.

Buoyed by the success of the festival, J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said, “It allowed a young writer meeting a director, an aspiring filmmaker learning from a professional or two people meeting here who may one day make a film together.”

Mr. Abdullah pitched Kashmir not “merely a filming destination” but “a place to emerge with stories”. “The festival was an idea being tested, an invitation, an experiment and, above all, a hope that Jammu and Kashmir could create a meaningful platform for cinema,” said Mr. Abdullah.

Referring to films shot in Kashmir in the past like ‘Aarzoo’, ‘Kashmir Ki Kali’ and ‘Kabhi Kabhi’, Mr. Abdullah said, “These films were screened against the very landscape that helped make them memorable.” These films were screened on a floating screen on the Dal lake.

“For decades, Kashmir travelled to audiences through a cinema screen. This week, in a sense, the screen came back to Kashmir,” said Mr. Abdullah.

Speaking on occasion, Union Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting, L Murugan, said J&K was emerging as an active creator, host and partner in modern global storytelling. “For decades, the silver screen showed us the snow peaks of Gulmarg, the saffron fields of Srinagar and the historic temples of Jammu through a camera lens. Today, J&K is not just a brief shooting location; it is becoming an active creator, host and partner in modern global storytelling,” said Mr. Murugan.

The concluding session of the festival was wrapped up by enthralling performances of singers Usha Uthup and Gulzar Ganai. Several movies, directors and actors were also awarded on the occasion. Filmmaker Kapil Matto’s ‘Tasrufdar – The Jinns of Kashmir’ bagged the award for Best Film in the J&K Category. Tanya Maniktala Wins Best Female Actress Award for ‘Arifa’.

World.title: Under-construction bridge collapses in Bihar’s Vaishali, seven injured
World.content:
Seven people were injured after part of an under-construction bridge collapsed in Bihar’s Vaishali district on Thursday (September 10, 2026). The bridge is part of the Bharatmala Pariyojana – a Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways scheme to build and improve India’s road networks.

The incident took place near Itwaripur village under Lalganj police station during the four-lane construction work. After receiving the information, Vaishali Superintendent of Police, Shubhank Mishra and Sub Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Gopal Mandal inspected the site.

“First aid was provided to all the injured, of whom 3 injured individuals have been referred to Sadar Hospital, Hajipur, for better treatment. The senior official who reached on the site has instructed the relevant officials to investigate the incident and the construction company’s compliance with the prescribed safety standards. Further action is being taken in connection with the incident, “Vaishali Police stated in its press release.

Out of seven, one worker remained trapped under the machine for about an hour and a half, due to which his leg got fractured. After much effort, the worker was safely rescued after using a gas cutter.

National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) also posted a message on its social media account X sharing the information about the incident.

“NHAI would like to inform that an incident occurred during the movement of a launching girder at an under-construction four-lane bridge on the Bakarpur–Manikpur section of NH-139W in Hajipur, Bihar, due to a technical issue in the launching girder system,” NHAI stated.

It further said, “A detailed technical assessment is currently underway to ascertain the circumstances that led to the malfunction. Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings of the assessment. NHAI accords the highest priority to the safety and well-being of workers and all stakeholders associated with the project, as well as all National Highway projects across the country.”

Leader of Opposition Tejashiw Yadav criticised the state government over the collapse of the beam launcher, alleging that substandard construction materials, poor quality, disregard for standards, irregularities in inspections, and the corrupt role of National Democratic Alliance (NDA) leaders are the main reasons behind the continuous bridge collapses in Bihar.

“Another bridge collapses in Bihar! In Vaishali district, reports indicate that nearly half a dozen labourers were trapped and injured after yet another under-construction bridge collapsed under the weight of corruption. As expected, the corrupt NDA government will once again cover up its corruption.,” Mr. Yadav alleged.

World.title: Noida workers’ stir: hold officials accountable for ‘illegal detention’, say lawyers and activists
World.content:
Officials should be held accountable for the continued “illegal detention” of activists and workers in connection with a stir seeking wage hikes in Noida in April, several lawyers, activists and professors demanded at the Press Club of India on Thursday.

The call came following the Allahabad High Court’s ruling on September 2 that quashed the detention of 25-year-old Delhi University law student Akriti Chaudhary under the National Security Act (NSA) in connection with the stir.

At least 15 workers and eight activists, including former journalist Satyam Verma against whom provisions of the NSA have also been invoked, continue to be in jail in cases filed by the Uttar Pradesh police.

The court had come down heavily on Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam, who had issued the order to detain Ms. Chaudhary. It observed that Ms. Roopam “desired to make an example” out of the petitioner.

Demanding accountability from officials involved in the case, senior journalist John Dayal said: “Even if it is the daughter of the CEC (Chief Election Commissioner) or the CJI (Chief Justice of India), they must be held accountable for their actions.”

“The court verdict in Akriti’s case questions the functioning of Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam and this applies to most officials across the country. Just as Swatantra Bhardwaj (who was arrested in connection with the alleged assault on the father of a student during a protest at Jantar Mantar in July) boasts about his crimes calling BJP leaders ‘big brothers’, U.P. Police functions with the arrogance that the government and administration are their ‘big brothers,” Mr. Dayal said, adding that police reforms are needed in the country.

Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan said the quashing of Ms. Chaudhary’s NSA detention is “symptomatic of the winds of change” blowing through the country. “The students, youth, and working people of the country are on the streets demanding accountability from the government and the administration. It has put more pressure on the judiciary to give judgments in favour of the people,” he said.

Keshaw, an activist associated with the Campaign for Release of Activists and Workers of Noida (CaRWAN), said the High Court flagged discrepancies in Ms. Chaudhary’s detention order and termed the State’s version a “concocted story”.

“The Commissioner of Police, Laxmi Singh, had claimed at the outset that they had ‘strong electronic and videographic evidence’ to nab the ‘masterminds’. Yet, even after five months we do not see any concrete evidence being presented against any of the activists or workers,” he said.

“DM Medha Roopam, who has been reprimanded and fined by the Allahabad High Court, has written in the same document in which she approved the NSA detention that the workers’ agitation can affect capital investment and portray a harmful image of the industrial area. Is she not declaring loyalty to the industrialists of Noida whose exploitation led to the workers taking to the streets in the first place?” he said.

Mr. Keshaw also referred to a video that surfaced in which U.P. Police can be allegedly seen planting the phone of a detained activist at her home. “During police custody, they brought Srishti to her home to ‘recover evidence’. The footage clearly shows them placing her already seized phone and a book in her house and ordering her to take it, so they can capture it on video. Seeing the cameras, they abort their mission and even try to break the cameras,” he said.

Other speakers, including former JNU professor Arun Kumar, and lawyer Manik Gupta, representing the activists in courts, said the government was not ready to accept that there was skyrocketing inflation in the country and worsening workers’ conditions, which led to the protest. “After what happened in the Strait of Hormuz, the prices of LPG cylinders went up in India. Workers who earn ₹10,000-12,000 a month cannot afford to buy cylinders,” Mr. Kumar said, adding that around 94% of workers in India are employed in the unorganised sector.

“Whenever we apply for bail, new sections and new FIRs are added. The NSA is invoked. The accused are brought to court after custodial torture, in chains,” Mr. Gupta alleged. “It is fortunate in the current regime in U.P. that they were not killed in an encounter. All grounds for invoking the NSA have fallen apart in the court. No claim is backed by evidence,” he said.

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs3.05, diesel by Rs5.37
World.content:
The government on Thursday increased the price of petrol by Rs3.05 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.37 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs370.80 per litre while HSD will cost Rs398.04 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 11 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: IMF mission due on Sept 23 for biannual review of Pakistan’s economic performance
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission is due to visit Pakistan on September 23 for a biannual review of the country’s economic performance and implementation of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) for the period ending June 30, 2026.

Pakistan is currently under a $7 billion, 37-month IMF programme , aimed at stabilising the economy through fiscal discipline, structural reforms, and measures to support long-term growth.

Official sources said that during an almost two-week visit ending in the first week of October, the IMF staff mission, led by Iva Petrova, would conduct the fourth review of the EFF and the third review of the RSF.

The mission would begin its visit with technical discussions at the State Bank of Pakistan, followed by meetings with the government’s sectoral teams, alongside a customary inaugural meeting with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.

The engagement would also examine policy implementation at the start of the fiscal year, particularly the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) ability and preparedness to meet its first-ever half-yearly revenue collection structural benchmark under an IMF programme, given the revenue machinery’s repeated large annual shortfalls.

This would also be the first review after the provincial governments surrendered more than Rs1.035 trillion of their National Finance Commission (NFC) shares to the Centre during the current fiscal year for national security and water resources, on top of the Rs1.8tr cash surplus separately committed under IMF pressure.

The programme’s performance against the fiscal targets as of end-June 2026 — the period under review — has mostly been on track, albeit with a major revenue shortfall and slippages in the policy matrix. These include the government’s intervention in commodity operations, particularly wheat and sugar, in violation of an IMF condition requiring the government to keep its hands off the commodities market.

Given the biannual reviews of the $7bn EFF and the $1.4bn RSF, the two sides will have to agree on past performance as well as forward-looking implementation plans.

Upon successful completion of the review, Pakistan will be eligible for the disbursement of about $1bn (760 million Special Drawing Rights) under the EFF and another $200m under the RSF by the end of November or early December.

Official reports suggest that while qualitative performance criteria on the fiscal and monetary sides were mostly on track, progress on economic governance reforms lagged far behind requirements. They suggested that only a couple of targets out of more than three dozen for improving economic governance during the January-June 2026 period had been met.

These targets were set by the prime minister after the IMF’s governance and corruption diagnostic assessment found serious shortcomings in efforts to combat corruption.

While the government had introduced reforms to ensure transparent procurement processes in state-owned entities (SOEs), direct contracting with SOEs without open competitive bidding continued unabated.

There were also reports of agencies issuing tenders after projects had been completed through preferred contractors, compromising competitive pricing and transparency. The rules aimed at ending such preferential treatment have yet to be passed.

Earlier in July, an IMF representative hailed Pakistan’s “strong” economic reforms carried out under the lender’s $7 billion loan programme.

IMF’s Resident Representative for Pakistan Mahir Binici noted that the country’s performance under the 2024 EFF had been “strong so far”, according to a press release issued by the SDPI on its guest lecture in Islamabad.

World.title: Parliament to debate new provinces next month, says minister
World.content:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Thursday that parliament was expected to debate the issue of new provinces next month.

Addressing the corporate sector in late July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had called for the creation of new provinces or administrative units, saying that the current system had “collapsed”.

“There is no National Assembly session this month; however, sessions of both the National Assembly and Senate are expected in October. The discussions will be held whenever the sessions are convened,” the minister said in a video statement.

Chaudhry reiterated that parliament was the “proper forum” for debating the issue of forming new provinces, adding that the debate would definitely be initiated.

“Parliament can hold a debate on any topic — the National Assembly has representation from all four provinces, while the Senate has equal representation from each province. Every decision made here would be taken after consultations with all political parties,” Chaudhry said.

He also expressed hope that a “healthy discussion” would be held on the topic during the upcoming session.

Chaudhry elaborated that the discussion on forming new provinces or federating units was not a debate about “inheriting fortunes”, while advising political parties against taking an emotional stance on the issue.

“I am hopeful that before making a decision on forming new provinces or administrative units in the provinces, we will bring forward Islamabad’s governance model as a formal act.

“While maintaining the federal status of Islamabad, we will form Islamabad’s first legislative assembly,” he stated.

He clarified that Islamabad could not become a province and was not going to be made a separate province. “We are talking about improving its governance model by upholding its federal status.”

The minister said the draft proposing governance changes — including a legislative body with all relevant institutions under the supervision of a chief executive or mayor in Islamabad — had been prepared by a five-member committee appointed by the prime minister.

“It is a very simple model. We did not prepare this draft with any personal contrivance; it was prepared after studying existing governance models in various capitals around the world and their applicable plans,” he added.

Chaudhry maintained that he was in contact with other political parties. “I will sit with them, share the draft and hold consultations, and all the positive recommendations will be incorporated into the draft.”

Islamabad’s bar, chamber of commerce, residents and intellectuals would also be consulted, he added.

In July, Naqvi had proposed a dialogue among all political parties to bring about reforms to the current governance system, while also calling for new provinces and urgent administrative reforms.

His comments had ignited an animated debate across the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation.

Additional reporting by Syed Irfan Raza

World.title: Trump administration proposes waiving grace period for H-1B holders after job loss
World.content:
The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online on Thursday.

Under the planned rule change, published in the Federal Register by the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), those with H-1B and certain other temporary work visas would have to leave the country as soon as their employment ends — a potential blow to top American tech companies that rely heavily on foreign workers.

It is the latest step by US President Donald Trump to limit legal migration since returning to office in January 2025. His administration has also introduced higher visa fees for skilled workers and recently paused immigrant visa appointments at US missions around the world while it implements a new training programme.

Companies impacted by the change could see some disruption, DHS wrote in its proposal, but it said the jobs could go to American workers instead. In some situations, immigrant workers who leave could potentially reapply if their employer petitions for them, it added.

“DHS presumes that they will either offer the same jobs to equally qualified US workers or go through the I-129 petition process depending on their workforce requirement,” the notice said.

The 60-day grace period, in place since 2017, allows foreign workers time to find another US job or get their affairs in order, whether selling a home or pulling children out of school before leaving the country.

H-1B visas, established by Congress in 1990, are especially critical for tech companies seeking talent from India and China, allowing them to fill roles where there is sometimes a lack of qualified US workers.

Consultancy companies such as Deloitte, PwC and Ernst and Young, as well as outsourcing giants like Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, HCL Tech and LTIMindtree, are top H-1B sponsors.

Lawyers for Berardi Immigration Law, which specialises in business-related immigration issues, said the move would “sharply compress the timeline HR teams have to manage layoffs and offboarding for foreign national employees”.

If implemented, the change would also apply to E-1 international trader visa holders; E-2 commercial vehicle operator visa holders; L-1 short-term work for executives or managers with international companies; O-1 visas for people “with an extraordinary ability” in science, sports or the arts; and TN professional workers.

It would also impact H-1B1 skilled worker visa holders from Singapore and Chile and E-3 speciality worker visa holders from Australia.

The rule is subject to a two-month public comment period before it can be enacted into law.

World.title: PM Shehbaz invites NA opposition leader Achakzai for consultation on new CEC
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken a practical step towards initiating dialogue between the government and the opposition by inviting National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai for mandatory consultations on the appointment of a new Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), a source close to the prime minister told Dawn on Thursday.

However, the opposition leader has so far not responded to the prime minister’s invitation.

Interestingly, the invitation was extended days before the PTI-led long march towards Islamabad on Sept 27.

“Yes, the prime minister invited him (Achakzai) for consultation,” the source said.

A few days ago, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, during an NA session, stressed the need for political harmony and stability and expressed the desire for the prime minister to initiate dialogue with the opposition by, as a first step, inviting the opposition leader for consultations on the appointment of a new CEC.

On the other hand, PTI kept mum on the matter. When a senior party leader was contacted, he was reluctant to comment on the prime minister’s invitation.

The five-year term of incumbent CEC Sikandar Sultan Raja expired on Jan 26, 2025. Raja has remained controversial since the ouster of the PTI government in April 2022 over what the opposition called his “support” for the PML-N-led government.

One of the main allegations levelled against Raja was that he had deprived PTI of its party symbol, the bat, in the 2024 elections.

His critics alleged that the denial of the party symbol was aimed not only at disadvantaging PTI by confusing voters, but also at allowing PTI-backed “independents” to later join the ruling coalition without risking disqualification. They also claimed that the move was intended to deprive PTI of its share of reserved seats.

Section 2A of Article 213 of the Constitution says: “The Prime Minister shall in consultation with the Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly, forward three names for appointment of the Commissioner to a Parliamentary Committee for hearing and confirmation of any one person.”

Section 2B says: “The Parliamentary Committee to be constituted by the Speaker shall comprise fifty per cent members from the Treasury Benches and fifty per cent from the Opposition Parties, based on their strength in Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament), to be nominated by the respective Parliamentary Leaders: Provided that in case there is no consensus between the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, each shall forward separate lists to the Parliamentary Committee for consideration which may confirm any one name.”

“Provided further that the total strength of the Parliamentary Committee shall be twelve members out of which one-third shall be from the Senate, and provided also that when the National Assembly is dissolved and vacancy occurs in the office of the Chief Election Commissioner, the total membership of the Parliamentary Committee shall consist of the members from the Senate only and the foregoing provisions of this clause shall, mutatis mutandis, apply.”

Earlier in August, Achakzai urged the prime minister in a letter to appoint a new chief election commissioner, along with two members representing Sindh and Balochistan.

The incumbent CEC Raja, along with Sindh and Balochistan ECP members, have now been in office for over a year after the expiry of their constitutionally mandated five-year terms.

The terms of the three officials ended on Jan 26, 2025. Under Article 215(4) of the Constitution, appointments to these posts were required within 45 days after the positions became vacant , i.e., by March 12, 2025.

However, a proviso inserted into Article 215(1) through the 26th Constitutional Amendment allows the CEC and members to continue until their successors are appointed. The incumbent CEC and two ECP members are serving under this provision.

World.title: NA panel irked over poor mobile services, seeks efforts to bring Apple to Pakistan
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication on Thursday expressed serious concern over the poor quality of mobile and internet services and decided to summon telecom companies (telcos) to seek direct answers over persistent network problems.

The committee was also informed by an official of the Engineering Development Board (EDB) that efforts were underway to seek tech giant Apple’s entry into Pakistan’s manufacturing market.

In its proceedings, the committee expressed concerns over the quality of mobile services, with chairman Aminul Haque remarking that subscribers had to dial a number three times just to make a call.

“The quality of mobile and internet services is deteriorating day by day after the spectrum auction instead of any improvement,” the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) lawmaker said.

The chairman then questioned the PTA about the fines imposed during the last six months, noting that the regulator issued show-cause notices and warning letters, but did not impose sufficient fines on telecom companies.

Committee members Zulfiqar Ali Bhatti, Ahmad Ateeq Anwar, Sadiq Memon and Dr Mahesh Kumar stressed that the root causes of poor mobile service were not being addressed and criticised the PTA for repeatedly giving the same response without improving the situation.

Committee member Shazia Fareed recalled she had received virtually no mobile signals during her stay at Islamabad’s Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

The committee made it clear that the PTA should perform its duties and inform the parliament if there was any obstacle preventing it from taking action. Members proposed summoning representatives of telcos and seeking explanations from them directly.

Meanwhile, PTA officials assured the committee that the authority continuously monitored mobile and internet services and conducted surveys in cities to assess service quality.

They said telcos were given 30 days to improve their service quality and networks, while the PTA could impose a maximum fine of Rs350 million.

PTA officials further said that telcos often obtained stay orders from courts against penalties, and that several cases were pending before the courts. They added that the Telecom Tribunal was functional, but its decisions had also been challenged before courts.

The authority maintained that service quality was improving after the launch of 5G and that rollout targets for telcos had been clearly defined. A PTA member informed the committee that the number of 5G sites in Karachi was increasing and had reached 279.

IT Secretary Zarar Hasham Khan told the committee that telcos had installed equipment meeting international standards, and the government had prioritised improved service quality over revenue generation during the 5G spectrum auction held in March.

The committee decided to summon telcos at its next meeting and directed the PTA to provide details of fines imposed on them and the amount recovered.

Committee seeks efforts for Apple’s entry in Pakistan

The committee also discussed efforts to bring Apple to Pakistan, with Haque questioning why the tech giant could not enter the country’s market when other international mobile companies were already operating.

EDB Chief Executive Officer Hammad Mansoor told the committee that negotiations were under way to bring Apple into the country.

He added that efforts were also being made to arrange a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Apple CEO John Ternus during the former’s upcoming visit to the United States.

Mansoor said that an Apple store had already been established in Pakistan and expressed optimism that the company would also enter the country’s manufacturing market.

The EDB chief informed the committee that 37 companies were currently manufacturing mobile phones in Pakistan, and that more than 35 million devices had been manufactured locally so far.

The committee was told that all major smartphone companies were manufacturing phones in Pakistan, except Apple.

Haq directed the IT ministry and the PTA to come prepared with detailed information at the next meeting, and to continue efforts to bring Apple to Pakistan.

Mobile phone tax issue discussed

The committee also discussed the issue of taxes on imported mobile phones, and the potential payment of levies in instalments.

A PTA member clarified that the authority had no role in placing mobile phone taxes or in developing a mechanism for payment of such taxes in instalments, as all the tax matters were the domain of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR).

Committee member Syed Ali Qasim Gilani said he raised the issue and also took up the matter of allowing consumers to pay the tax in instalments.

He said the FBR had informed him that the mechanism was available with the PTA, but questioned how the authority could develop an instalment mechanism when it did not collect the tax.

The IT secretary said the issue of mobile phone tax instalments was not in his knowledge and assured the committee that he would discuss it with the PTA chairman and brief the committee, which sought a detailed briefing on the matter at its next meeting.

“Our vision should be smartphones for all,” Haque said, pointing out that a good quality phone was available in Pakistan for around Rs60,000.

Telecom sector seeks industrial tariff

Additionally, the committee also discussed the issue of electricity supplied to telecom infrastructure and the demand for industrial tariffs for telecom companies.

IT ministry’s Muhammad Jahanzeb, also a committee member, informed that his ministry had requested the Power Division to ensure uninterrupted electricity to telecom towers, noting that the sector had been declared an industry in 2004, while the 2021 Finance Act had also recognised telecom as an industry.

The ministry also informed the committee that interruptions in telecom services caused by load-shedding were affecting freelancers and a large segment of the population.

However, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) had refused to extend industrial tariff to the telecom sector, he said.

“Twenty-two years have passed since 2004, but a government institution is still not accepting it,” PPP’s Memon remarked.

The IT secretary said the government had tried to protect telecom towers from load-shedding, but the Power Division had made it clear that providing dedicated feeders to telecom towers was not possible.

Haque maintained that the telecom sector should be granted the status of an industry and announced that Nepra would also be summoned before the committee.

The committee decided to summon Nepra and Power Division officials to discuss the issue.

It also directed the IT ministry to complete the required paperwork regarding the industrial status and tariff issue.

World.title: Algeria severs diplomatic ties with UAE over ‘provocative, hostile’ actions
World.content:
Algeria said on Thursday it had decided to sever diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) after what it described as a series of “provocative or hostile” actions by Abu Dhabi despite “repeated warnings”.

The Algerian foreign ministry said the UAE’s actions had reached a point where they could no longer be considered acceptable or tolerable and that it had “exhausted all means of preserving bilateral relations.”

The UAE ambassador was summoned to the ministry, informed of the decision and given 48 hours to comply, the foreign ministry said.

The UAE Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.

Relations between the two countries have come under growing strain in recent years, with Algerian media outlets sharply criticising the UAE and accusing it of seeking to sow regional discord.

Algiers and Abu Dhabi have also taken differing positions on several regional issues. Algeria opposes normalisation with Israel, while the UAE and Algeria’s regional rival Morocco established diplomatic ties with Israel under the US-brokered Abraham Accords in 2020.

The two countries are also on opposing sides of the decades-old Western Sahara dispute. The UAE supports Morocco’s claim to sovereignty over the territory where it has a consulate, while Algeria backs the Polisario Front, which seeks an independent Western Sahara.

The two countries’ interests have increasingly intersected in the Sahel, where the UAE has expanded ties with several governments in recent years, while Algeria’s relations with some of its southern neighbours have become strained following a series of military coups.

Algerian President Abdelmadjid said last year his country’s relations with all Gulf states were warm except for one — a thinly veiled reference to the UAE.

He described ties with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar as “brotherly”, while accusing the unnamed country of meddling in Algeria’s internal affairs and seeking to destabilise it.

In February, Algeria began the process of cancelling an air services agreement with the UAE that was signed in Abu Dhabi in May 2013.

World.title: 'Is judiciary so weak that you wish to strengthen it?' IHC CJ asks as KP counsel justifies PTI’s Sept 27 march
World.content:
